## Summary

Measure whether the child-port discovery fix (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF, deployed
2026-10-26T21:01Z) actually eliminates router-responder `GET /slots ... 500`
responses over a full 24 h production window, and record the raw counts as
auditable evidence.

**Earliest run: 2026-10-27T12:00Z.** Window:
**2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z.** If the fix (or a follow-up restart)
lands later than that, shift the window to start 24 h after the last relevant
deployment and record the new timestamps in a comment.

**Window state verified at planning (2026-10-28T04:40Z):** the window is
**still open** (≈7 h 20 m remaining at verification time). Production facts:
proxy pid **3791954** started **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** and is still running
(18 h 23 m uptime) — the fixed proxy has been up continuously since **before**
the window opened, and **no proxy restart has occurred inside the window**, so
the AC6 restart condition is satisfiable. No pre-window baseline comment was
recorded at 12:00Z; see "Baseline reconstruction" under the execute-time plan
for why the counter delta is nonetheless provable.

## Problem statement

Router-proxied `GET /slots` polls returned HTTP 500 at ~9 % during giant
prefills because child-port discovery silently failed and every proxy poll
traversed the router. The fix replaced discovery with a rotation-proof signal
and routed every call site through it, but the only proof that matters is a
production 24 h window with zero such 500s — the pre-fix evidence (1,754
router 500s in the 2026-10-26 log) is not proof of absence.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainer** — "As the operator, I want a dated, reproducible
  measurement of router-responder `/slots` 500s so I can close the residual-500
  bug and trust the fix, instead of re-reading raw logs myself."
- **On-call agent (herdr downtime worker)** — "As an unattended agent, I want a
  deterministic method and explicit verdict rule so my pass/fail report does
  not depend on my own judgement of ambiguous counts."
- **Downstream users** — chat/agent clients that see 500s and 5–7 s slot-poll
  latency when slot queries serialise behind a busy child.

## Acceptance Criteria

Refined at intake per producer decisions Q1(a), Q2(b), Q3(a):

- **AC1** — **Chat-model path: zero.** The windowed count of router-responder
  `GET /slots ... 500` responses attributable to the chat model is **0**.
  Responder split: lines with no `[pid]` prefix are the router, `[pid]`-prefixed
  lines are the model children; per-file counts are reported for every
  `llama-server*.log` file whose mtime falls inside the window (Q1a).
- **AC2** — **Raw router and child counts reported**, so a silent switch back to
  router polling cannot masquerade as a pass: router-responder `GET /slots`
  200 / 400 / 500 and model-child 200 / 400 / 500 counts for each file in the
  window. `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` output is attached verbatim.
- **AC3** — **`slots_stale` share reported** for `status_request` polls in the
  window: the primary figure is *all* `status_request` polls (directly
  comparable to the pre-fix baseline **579/899** in the 2026-10-26 file), with
  the active-prefill subset (`active_query=true` or `local_active_query=true`)
  reported as a secondary figure (Q3a).
- **AC4** — **Fallback evidence reported, split by path** (Q2b):
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  delta across the window plus the (throttled, undercounting)
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning lines, attributed by model.
  - Chat-model (`Qwen3`) fallbacks: **any occurrence fails the check.**
  - Embed-model (`mxbai-embed`) fallbacks: reported separately as a
    **non-blocking observation**; if any occur, a new bug item is filed at
    window end, linked `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`.
- **AC5** — **Reproducibility:** the exact commands/regexes (or script
  invocations) used, the window start/end timestamps, the pre-window baseline
  snapshot (counter values, log line count, proxy pid + start time) and the raw
  counts are all recorded as a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — **Restart integrity:** any proxy restart inside the window is
  detected (pid change) and reported; if one occurred, the counter delta is
  declared unavailable and the verdict relies on per-file log counts with the
  limitation stated explicitly.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Method (agreed: Q1 option (a) — hybrid)

Measured with existing tooling plus two log families:

```bash
# 1. Window-start snapshot (also record: date -u, pid start time, log line count)
date -u; ps -o lstart= -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app')"
wc -l < /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'

# 2. Window-end snapshot (same commands, 24 h later) -> counter delta = exact
#    windowed fallbacks when the proxy was not restarted in between.

# 3. Responder/status split per file (reuses the triage CLI: no timestamps in
#    llama-server logs, so scope by the files whose mtime falls in the window)
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --llama-file 'llama-server.log' --summary

# 4. Fallback warnings (throttled to one line per interval -> undercounts;
#    the counter above is authoritative)
grep -c 'slots_child_port_unavailable' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log

# slots_stale share (existing baseline method)
grep -o 'slots_stale=[a-z]*' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log | sort | uniq -c
```

Take a **pre-window baseline snapshot** immediately before
2026-10-27T12:00Z (counter values + `llama-server.log` line count + proxy pid
start time) so the window delta is unambiguous.

> **Status: not done.** No snapshot comment exists for 2026-10-27T12:00Z. The
execution plan below reconstructs the baseline from monotonic-counter
evolution plus pid `lstart`, and states the limitation explicitly (AC5).

## Execution plan (exact recipe — run at/after 2026-10-28T12:00Z)

Steps 0–2 must be re-verified at run time, not trusted from this block; they
are read-only and cheap. Steps 3–6 produce the evidence; step 7 records it.

### Step 0 — window gate

Do **not** measure before **2026-10-28T12:00Z**. An earlier run measures a
partial window and is not acceptable as the AC evidence.

### Step 1 — restart integrity (AC6)

```bash
date -u
ps -o pid,lstart,etime -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app' | head -1)"
```

Expected: a single pid **3791954** with `lstart` **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** ⇒ no
restart inside the window. Any other pid/`lstart` ⇒ record the restart time,
declare the counter delta unavailable, and fall back to per-file log counts
with the limitation stated (AC6).

### Step 2 — fallback counter (AC4, exact)

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'
```

A Prometheus counter that has never been incremented emits **no sample line**
(only `# HELP` / `# TYPE`). That is the state observed at planning — quote the
raw output verbatim, because "absent sample" is the auditable form of "0".
Range-vector deltas are not needed: a monotonic counter reading 0 on a process
that started before the window ⇒ windowed delta = 0.

### Baseline reconstruction (AC5, replaces the missed 12:00Z snapshot)

State the limitation explicitly and rebuild the baseline from: proxy pid +
`lstart` (step 1); the counter's never-incremented state (step 2); the per-file
line counts read at window end. The proof is monotonicity, not a start sample:
the process started 1 h 44 m before the window opened and its counter is still
0.

### Step 3 — llama-server file set (AC1 / AC2)

```bash
ls -l --time-style=full-iso /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server*.log*
```

Window set (mtime inside 2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z):
`llama-server.log-2026-10-28` (logrotate `copytruncate` copy at 00:00Z; content
= 2026-10-27T00:00Z → 2026-10-28T00:00Z) and the live `llama-server.log`
(content = 2026-10-28T00:00Z → window end). `llama-server.log-2026-10-27.gz`
has mtime 2026-10-27T00:00Z ⇒ outside the window, exclude it.

llama-server access lines carry **no timestamps**, so this union covers
2026-10-27T00:00Z → window end: a **superset** of the window, carrying 12 h of
extra pre-window traffic. Consequence: **zero router-responder 500s across the
superset proves zero inside the window** (report the over-count direction); a
non-zero count needs the per-file split plus the caveat that the window
boundary is approximate at ±12 h granularity.

```bash
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --llama-file 'llama-server.log-2026-10-28' --summary
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --llama-file 'llama-server.log' --summary
```

Record both per-file outputs verbatim (AC2) and sum the responder/status matrix
(router 200/400/500, child 200/400/500).

### Step 4 — proxy.log file set (AC3, plus AC4 warnings)

`proxy.log` is timestamped and self-rotates every 6 h, and the daily
`copytruncate` copy (`proxy.log-YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) can duplicate a range — so
**file names do not reliably delimit the window**. Derive each candidate's own
first/last timestamp from its lines, keep the parts intersecting the window,
and dedupe overlapping ranges (keep one generation per timestamp range):

```bash
for f in /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*; do
  case "$f" in *.gz) zcat "$f";; *) cat "$f";; esac \
    | awk -v f="$f" 'NR==1{first=$0} {last=$0} END{print f"	"substr(first,1,19)"	"substr(last,1,19)}'
done
```

At planning time the window-relevant generations were
`proxy.log.2026-10-27_10`, `proxy.log.2026-10-27_16`, `proxy.log.2026-10-27_22`,
`proxy.log-2026-10-28_00` and the live `proxy.log` — indicative only; re-derive
the set from timestamps at run time.

```bash
# AC3 primary: all status_request polls in the window (comparable to 579/899)
grep -h 'status_request' <window files> | grep -o 'slots_stale=[a-z]*' | sort | uniq -c
# AC3 secondary: active-prefill subset
grep -h 'status_request' <window files> \
  | grep -o 'active_query=[a-z]*\|local_active_query=[a-z]*' | sort | uniq -c
# AC4 warnings, per file (throttled -> undercounts; the step-2 counter is authoritative)
for f in <window files>; do printf '%s	' "$f"; grep -c 'slots_child_port_unavailable' "$f"; done
grep -h 'slots_child_port_unavailable' <window files>   # attribute each by model=
```

### Step 5 — verdict rule

**GREEN** ⇔ chat-model router-responder `/slots` 500s = 0 **and** chat-model
fallback delta = 0 (counter **and** warning lines). Embed-model
(`mxbai-embed`) occurrences are reported separately and file a linked bug
(`discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`) without ever making the verdict RED.
Any other positive chat-model count ⇒ **RED**: name the model/responder and
file the linked bug. Report router/child 200/400 counts and the `slots_stale`
share alongside either way (AC2/AC3).

### Step 6 — evidence comment (AC5)

One comment recording: window start/end; `date -u` at run time; pid + `lstart`
+ uptime; the raw `/metrics` line(s); both per-file triage outputs verbatim;
the `proxy.log` file set with each file's observed first/last timestamp; the
dedupe/overlap rule applied; the counts; the `slots_stale` primary and
active-prefill figures; the "llama-server lines are timestamp-free ⇒ ±12 h
boundary approximation" caveat; the missed-baseline limitation; the verdict;
and any linked bug id.

AC7 and AC8 are code-change boilerplate on a measurement item — see the OPEN
QUESTION in the Appendix for the interpretation used.

## Existing state (evidence gathered at intake, 2026-10-26T23:36Z)

- **Fix is deployed.** Proxy pid 3482545 restarted 2026-10-26T21:01:42Z
  (after fix commits `f58e8964` 2026-10-26T12:51Z and `189864fc`
  2026-10-26T13:00Z, both on `dev`). Blocking item LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF is
  `completed`/`in_review`. _(Superseded 2026-10-27T10:16:11Z: pid 3482545 was
  replaced by pid **3791954**, still running at planning time. Both fix commits
  are ancestors of `dev`. The restart predates the window, so the window is
  restart-free.)_
- **Early signal the chat path is fixed.** Live 90 s spot check at
  23:36Z: 78 model-responder `/slots` events, **0** router-responder `/slots`
  events, 0 HTTP 500s.
- **Residual fallbacks exist post-fix.** `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  is already **4** since the 21:01:42Z restart, and one throttled
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING was logged at **21:01:46Z** for
  `model=mxbai-embed` (the embedding child). The current `llama-server.log`
  also still holds ~4 router-responder `/slots` lines in its last ~25 min.
  Consequence: AC4's "one occurrence fails" will very likely trip on
  restart/embed transients — resolved as Q2 option (b).
- **Rotation breaks the single-file method.** `llama-server.log` is rotated
  in-process (`rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)`, numeric `llama-server.N.log`) and
  by the `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` safety net (daily, `copytruncate`,
  `dateext` → `llama-server.log-YYYY-MM-DD`). `proxy.log` self-rotates every
  6 h (`proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HH`). A 24 h window therefore spans several
  files, and llama-server access lines carry **no timestamps**
  (`scripts/slots_500_triage.py` documents this: "no timestamps in
  llama-server logs; the corpus is per-file"). A single-file grep cannot
  cover the window — resolved at intake as Q1 option (a), hybrid.
- **Cumulative figures today** (`--llama-file 'llama-server.log'`, whole
  file, spans more than one day and predates the fixed restart):
  router 200 = 38,369; router 400 = 452; router 500 = 2,753; model 200 /
  child 200 = 68,610 + 8. Non-zero router 200s show that **direct LAN clients
  poll the router** legitimately, so raw router counts are not pure
  proxy-fallback evidence.
- **`slots_stale` alive in the current `proxy.log`**: 2,019 false / 1,952 true
  (49 % true) since the current file began — usable as an intermediate
  reference, not the window figure.
- **No existing windowed tool.** `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` classifies by
  responder/status and supports `--llama-file <glob>`, but has no
  `--since/--until`; window scoping is a manual file-set decision.

## Desired change

No product code change: this item is a **measurement and evidence** task. Its
"change" is a recorded, reproducible verdict (counts, commands, window
timestamps, and either a green pass or a new linked bug when red).

**Verdict rule (agreed):** GREEN = windowed chat-model router-responder
`/slots` 500s are 0 **and** the chat-model fallback delta is 0, with router and
child 200/400 counts and the `slots_stale` share reported alongside. RED = any
positive chat-model count; a RED verdict must name the model/responder and
create a linked bug item (`discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`). Embed-model
fallbacks never make the verdict RED — they raise a linked bug instead.

## Constraints

- Window must be a full 24 h with the fixed proxy running; restarts inside the
  window must be detected and reported (they reset counters).
- No production restart, no config change, and no code change is needed for the
  measurement itself (`start-proxy` must not be invoked unless the proxy dies).
- llama-server logs are timestamp-free → any time attribution is per-file and
  approximate; this limitation must be stated in the recorded comment, never
  silently smoothed over.
- If the verdict is red, a new bug item is created (linked
  `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`); LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF is never silently
  reopened.
- Measurement must not perturb the proxy: read-only log greps plus a single
  `/metrics` scrape at start and end.
- **Execution gate (recorded at planning, 2026-10-28T04:40Z):** the window
  closes at **2026-10-28T12:00Z**; a run started earlier measures a partial
  window and must not be used as the AC evidence. Assignee `Map` is the
  scheduling hold — clear it at/after 2026-10-28T12:00Z to release the item.

## Key Files

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — existing responder/status classifier; needs a windowed (file-set) invocation or a documented file-selection recipe.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_discover_local_child_port`, `_resolve_local_slots_target`, `_warn_child_port_fallback` (emits `slots_child_port_unavailable`; throttled).
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` counter (exact, reset on restart).
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)` in-process numeric rotation (file boundaries = restarts).
- `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` — daily `copytruncate`/`dateext` safety net for both log families.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` (+ `llama-server.N.log`, `llama-server.log-YYYY-MM-DD`) — router vs child `/slots` access lines.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` (+ `proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) — `slots_stale`, `status_request`, `slots_child_port_unavailable`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (high): verdict goes red on embed-model transients.** Post-fix
  counter already 4 with one `mxbai-embed` warning in ~2.5 h of uptime; a
  literal AC4 makes the window almost certainly red for a cause that is not
  the busy-child 500 storm. **Resolved (Q2b):** embed fallbacks are reported
  separately and never make the verdict RED; a linked bug is filed instead.
- **Risk (medium): coverage gap.** If a rotation/restart lands mid-window, the
  single-file greps under-report. **Resolved (Q1a):** counter delta plus
  file-set aggregation, restart-aware (AC6).
- **Risk (medium): attribution.** Direct LAN clients polling the router
  produce router 200/400/500s that are not proxy-fallback symptoms; without
  source attribution the check can be red for unrelated noise. **Mitigation
  (agreed):** the fallback counter is the primary chat-path signal; raw router
  counts are reported for masquerade detection only, with the limitation
  stated in the recorded comment.
- **Risk (low): timing slip.** The 12:00Z window needs an agent at both ends;
  a late start truncates the window. Mitigation: snapshot first, then wait.
- **Assumption:** "the fix is deployed" means proxy pid started after
  `189864fc`; re-verify pid start time at window start rather than trusting
  this brief.
- **Scope-creep guard:** a reusable windowed measurement script (e.g.
  `--since/--until` on `slots_500_triage.py`) is a **separate follow-up item**,
  not part of this measurement.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF** — Residual router-proxied `/slots` 500s: audit
  remaining call sites and enforce direct child-port polling (completed; the
  fix under test here).
- **LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8** — Router `/slots` HTTP 400s: `?model=` resolution
  path (86 residual router 400 responses) — sibling split, shares AC2's 400
  reporting.
- **LP-0MTCMEV1G0022A35** — `/slots` 500-storm triage tooling
  (`scripts/slots_500_triage.py`), reused here.
- **LP-0MTIHZ8M5005ZAU8** — earlier (inert) direct-child fix; historical
  context for why the rotation-proof signal was needed.
- **LP-0MTDGBRPU003Z7KU** — 5–7 s router-proxied slot-poll latency measurement
  (the latency symptom of the same defect).
- Automated find-related report: work items LP-0MQYEY34L000H3O8 (ui.py
  `_extract_router_model_ids` NameError), LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P (proxy logger
  output), LP-0MQ6EGGJ6002JHZX (single-model mode) — same log/proxy surface,
  no AC overlap.

## Interview decisions (resolved)

- **Q1 = (a) Hybrid window scoping.** Fallback-counter delta from `/metrics` at
  window start/end (exact, restart-aware) + `scripts/slots_500_triage.py`
  counts summed across every `llama-server*.log` file whose mtime falls in the
  window, reported per-file with the "llama-server lines are timestamp-free →
  approximate attribution" caveat. No code change; a `--since/--until` upgrade
  to the triage CLI stays a separate follow-up item.
- **Q2 = (b) Chat-model zero tolerance, embed reported separately.** `Qwen3`
  path: zero router-responder 500s and zero fallbacks. `mxbai-embed` fallbacks
  are a non-blocking observation and spawn a linked bug at window end if any
  occur.
- **Q3 = (a) All `status_request` polls as the primary `slots_stale`
  denominator**, with the active-prefill subset as a secondary figure.

Source: producer reply "As recommended" (2026-10-27T00:48Z, accepting the three
recommended options in comment LP-C0MVPWPEKW004SSKP).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (plan, 2026-10-28T04:40Z)** — AC7 ("all related
  documentation updated … README, wiki or docs site entries") and AC8 ("full

## Goal

Convert the measured window (sibling measurement item) into the AC3 closure verdict for the tracking item LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I, keep the parent-AC4 evidence trail current, and re-point the ownership link now that the scheduler epic has landed without removing the residual.

## Context

- **AC1 is already recorded.** The parent AC4 re-scope comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D (2026-10-25T20:39) references this item and the 12 user-traffic events / 7.4 h measurement with the audit split. Re-confirm it against the fresh window.
- **AC2's edge is mechanically satisfied but stale.** The depends-on edge to LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG exists and the epic is completed, yet the residual survived it. At intake the live fix owner was recorded as LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (predicted-warmth / `measured_cache_deficit` early abort), whose F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD owned the fix's own post-deploy measurement. **Updated at the verdict (2026-10-30):** both are terminal (Option D live from the 2026-10-29T00:10:19Z restart; F5's post-deploy window measured under LP-0MVS03KCV005BTGE) and the residual survived them — 47 user-class `prefill_deadline` evictions in the 24 h post-deploy window. The live mechanism owner is now **LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2** (abandoned-prefill backlog); see *Relationships* below.
- **AC4's rollback note is in the description.** Re-affirm it with the fresh window's numbers.

## Scope

**In:** the AC3 verdict; the AC3(b) producer re-scope proposal when path (a) fails; evidence, link and rollback recording on this item and in a parent-AC4 comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D; description updates limited to the Ownership / Relationships / Key Files lines that the measurements proved stale.

**Out:** any code change; any change to parent AC4 text or thresholds without explicit producer approval (AC3(b)); measurement work (the sibling measurement item).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Parent AC1 (Evidence recorded).** "**AC1 — Evidence recorded.** The 22-event/7.4 h measurement (12 user-traffic) with the `progress=0` signature and the audit-load split is referenced from the parent AC4 comment." — re-confirmed with the post-occupancy-fix window and referenced from a parent AC4 comment.
- **AC2 — Parent AC2 (Link established).** "**AC2 — Link established.** A related edge points to LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG so the producer can fold this into the scheduler scope (or explicitly re-scope parent AC4 to exclude audit traffic / warm-HOL)." — recorded as satisfied (depends-on edge present; epic completed 2026-10-25T23:44Z).
- **AC2b — Successor link recorded.** Because the residual survived the scheduler epic, the live fix owner LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (with its F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD) is recorded as the successor link in this item's description and a related-to comment — not as a `wl dep add` edge, which would set this item `blocked` before its own verdict work can run — and the superseded occupancy hypothesis is stated explicitly.
- **AC3 — Parent AC3 (Closure).** "**AC3 — Closure.** Closed only when either (a) the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance, or (b) the producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and the re-scoped criterion is met." — a written verdict records which path applies: either (a) is certified from the measurement window, or (a) fails and an AC3(b) re-scope proposal (recommended user-traffic threshold, rationale and measurement plan) is put to the producer with `wl reviewed LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I true`. No parent AC4 text, threshold or AC is changed without an explicit producer reply recorded on this item; the item closes only on the matching condition.
- **AC4 — Parent AC4 (Rollback note).** "**AC4 — Rollback note.** No rollback recommended: the budget change is working (−88 % deadline rate, 0 over-budget admissions, −83 % wasted tokens); rolling back restores the thrash without touching this residual." — re-affirmed with the fresh window's numbers and recorded on this item and in the parent AC4 comment.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` (`EVICTION_REASONS`, `log_local_eviction`) — the closed reason vocabulary the verdict reports against
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (`ProjectedWait`, `evaluate_admission`) — the admission maths the rollback note refers to
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` — the window evidence the verdict cites
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — the analyser that produces every figure the verdict cites (same classifier as the parent AC4 measurement)
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md` and `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-2026-10-29.json` — the recorded report and per-event dataset (commit `56d853be`)

## Relationships (successor links, recorded 2026-10-30 — AC2b)

The residual survived the scheduler epic **and** the Option D fix, so the fix ownership is re-pointed here. Recorded as this description plus a related-to comment, deliberately **not** as a `wl dep add` edge: a dependency on a non-terminal item would set this verdict item `blocked` before its own recording work can run.

- **Superseded fix owner:** LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (Option D `measured_cache_deficit` early abort, F4 `1908f431`) with F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD and its post-deploy delegate LP-0MVS03KCV005BTGE — all terminal; their own ≥24 h post-deploy window still shows 47 user-class `prefill_deadline` evictions.
- **Live mechanism owner (successor):** LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — an early-released dispatch keeps prefilling in `llama-server` and starves the next dispatch (26 % of the day's prefill compute thrown away; 58 of the 60 measured events started inside an abandoned-prefill window). Discovered from the measurement item LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O.
- **Predecessor evidence:** LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O (measured window, `completed` — this item's blocker, satisfied).
- **Parent-AC4 owner:** LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D — its AC4 carries the residual clause; the refreshed evidence comment was posted there with this verdict.
- **Superseded hypothesis, stated explicitly:** second-slot head-of-line blocking (a warm prompt blocked behind another session's prefill) is **superseded** — it explains 9 of 60 events (15 %), and none of those 9 had another session's lease extended inside its window. The dominant cause (43 of 60, 72 %) is predicted-but-unmeasured warmth: priced at ~95 % cached (`p50` priced cached ratio 0.946), zero backend prefill progress for the whole 120 s lease, and a retry that re-enters at the same price — kept alive by the abandoned-prefill backlog.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — producer availability.** AC3(b) needs an explicit producer reply; if none arrives the item stays open with the question recorded (AC3).
- **Risk — stale-link confusion.** Recording the successor link as a `wl dep add` edge would set this item `blocked`; the description/comment form in AC2b preserves dispatchability at the cost of a softer link.
- **Risk — re-scope fatigue.** The parent AC4 has already been re-scoped once (2026-10-25); the AC3(b) proposal must state why a further re-scope is warranted rather than assuming it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the sibling measurement item. The closure certification also needs LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (fix) and its F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD (post-deploy measurement) to be terminal; this is recorded as a stated prerequisite rather than a `wl dep add` edge so the recording work remains dispatchable.

## Deliverables

A verdict comment on this item (path (a) certified, or (a)-fails plus the AC3(b) proposal), the parent-AC4 evidence comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D, and the re-affirmed rollback note.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator I need a **measured, reproducible verdict** on whether
`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` (the `amd_gpu_metrics_v3_0` blob, the
interface `amdgpu_top` reads) carries a *graded* GFX-activity signal on this
Strix Halo APU — one that separates compute from idle the way the
power-derived `gpu:computing:bool` rule does but `gpu_busy_percent` does not —
and, only if such a field passes an explicit discrimination bar, to have it
published as a Prometheus series through the existing 10 s textfile sampler.
A negative verdict, recorded with numbers so the path is never retried, is an
equally valid outcome.

## Problem statement

The usage report's GPU busy time infers activity from power draw
(`gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`), which cannot tell GFX work from any other
power draw. `gpu_busy_percent` was eliminated as a utilisation signal
(2026-10-28: 45.2 % false-busy, Pearson r = 0.28 against power,
LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL), leaving `gpu_metrics` as the last candidate hardware
activity source. **Intake measurements (2026-10-29) show that candidate is very
probably dead too**: `average_gfx_activity` read **100 % on every one of 120
samples across two captures** while package power moved between 42 W and 123 W
and DRAM bandwidth between 0.7 and 59.5 GB/s. This item therefore exists to
settle the question with evidence and a stated bar, not to assume the answer.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Is the GPU actually doing work right now, and was it
  busy between 17:00 and 19:00?" — needs a utilisation figure that is a direct
  measurement, not a power-draw proxy.
- **Agent answering a usage/incident question (secondary).** Needs to know which
  hardware fields are trustworthy on this host so it cites a real signal instead
  of re-litigating `gpu_busy_percent`.

User stories:

- As an operator I can run one command that decodes `gpu_metrics`, samples it
  alongside power and `gpu_busy_percent`, and prints per-field discrimination
  statistics — so the verdict rests on numbers I can reproduce.
- As an operator I am told plainly whether the interface gives a graded signal,
  with the capture date, kernel, sample counts and band means, so I never
  re-investigate it.
- As an operator, if a field does pass, the series appears next to the existing
  `gpu_*` textfile series without a new daemon, port or scrape job.

## Existing state (measured during intake, 2026-10-29, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic)

| Question | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Is the file live and readable? | `-r--r--r-- 4096` root:root; 264 bytes of content; values change between reads; no root, no ROCm, no `amd-smi` needed |
| Which structure? | Header decodes to `structure_size=264, format_revision=3, content_revision=0` → `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`; the same header text is vendored in `libdrm_amdgpu_sys`'s `wrapper_gpu_metrics.h`) |
| Does the layout check out? | Field sizes under `#pragma pack(4)` sum to 260 B; 4 B tail padding = **264 B**, matching `structure_size` exactly. Cross-checks: `average_socket_power` 95 060 mW vs hwmon `power1_average` 95.06 W (0.1 % agreement); `average_gfx_power` 11.3–44.2 W; `average_gfxclk_frequency` 2 711–2 900 MHz; `average_dram_reads` 0.7–59.5 GB/s; `average_vcn_activity` 0; `average_ipu_activity` all 0; `temperature_gfx` 56–69 °C |
| Does the activity field discriminate? | **No.** Capture A (60 samples @1 s): power 44–123 W, DRAM 1.8–59.5 GB/s → `average_gfx_activity` = 100 on all 60. Capture B (60 samples @1 s): power 42–66 W (idle band), DRAM 0.7–3.5 GB/s → 100 on all 60. Spot samples earlier: 97, 99, 100 at 41–57 W |
| How does it compare with the rejected counter? | Identically saturated: `gpu_busy_percent` = 100 on all 120 samples of both captures; `rocm-smi --showuse` reports `GPU use 100 %` at 54 W. GFX clock is pinned at its 2 900 MHz maximum in *both* bands, so the GFX domain is never gated while the proxy holds the device |
| What *does* vary with load? | `average_dram_reads`/`average_dram_writes` (memory bandwidth, 0.7 → 59.5 GB/s), `average_gfx_power` (11.3 → 44.2 W), `average_socket_power` (42 → 123 W), `average_core_c0_activity` (per-core C0 residency) |
| Are the values instantaneous? | No — they are SMU **time filtered** (`time_filter_alphavalue` = 1 000 000); the filter window is undocumented, so no claim finer than the sample interval is supportable |

Existing pipeline this would plug into: `gpu-metrics.service` runs
`~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` every 10 s, writing `gpu.prom` into
node_exporter's textfile collector (`gpu_busy_percent`, `gpu_vram_*`,
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes`, label `gpu="card0"`), scraped every 15 s by Prometheus;
documented in [docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service](../../docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service)
and [monitoring/README.md](../../monitoring/README.md).

## Desired change

1. **A reproducible probe CLI** — `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py`: decode the
   v3.0 blob from a sysfs path (default
   `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`), sample every candidate activity
   field alongside the two reference signals (amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` and
   `gpu_busy_percent`) at a configurable interval for a configurable duration,
   and emit CSV or `--json`. A `--verdict` mode prints the per-field
   discrimination statistics against the bar below.
2. **A recorded verdict** — the measured numbers plus a pass/fail decision per
   candidate field, written into the work item and the two monitoring documents,
   so the interface is either adopted once or closed off permanently.
3. **Conditional publication** — only if a field passes the bar, publish it
   through the existing 10 s textfile sampler (new `# HELP`/`# TYPE` series with
   the `gpu="card0"` label, atomic write, nothing written on read failure). If
   nothing passes, publish nothing and record why.
4. **A regression guard** — a saturated activity field must not be usable as a
   utilisation input in any rule or report query without a test failing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decodes `gpu_metrics` into named fields
  using the pinned v3.0 layout and validates the header
  (`structure_size` == layout size, `format_revision` == 3); unit tests cover a
  real 264-byte capture committed as a fixture, a truncated buffer, and an
  unknown `format_revision`/`structure_size`, which must be rejected with a
  clear error rather than misparsed.
- [ ] A capture (`--duration`/`--interval`, defaults documented) writes one row
  per sample containing a timestamp, every candidate activity field,
  `power1_average_watts` and `gpu_busy_percent`; a test drives the sampler
  against fixture sysfs trees (fake `/sys/class/drm/card0/device` and hwmon
  directory) and asserts row count, monotonic timestamps and fixture-derived
  values, without sleeping.
- [ ] `--verdict` reports, per candidate field, the idle-band mean (< 60 W), the
  compute-band mean (≥ 90 W), their separation in percentage points, Pearson r
  against package power, and the idle-band false-busy share (samples ≥ 90 %
  while power < 60 W); a field passes only if separation ≥ 30 pp **and**
  r ≥ 0.6 **and** idle-band false-busy ≤ 10 %. Unit tests drive synthetic
  saturated, graded and noisy series and assert the exact pass/fail decision and
  the printed statistics.
- [ ] The measured numbers and the resulting verdict — positive **or** negative
  — are recorded in `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`,
  `monitoring/README.md` (the "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`?"
  section gains a `gpu_metrics` row) and the work item, including capture date,
  kernel version, sample counts and band statistics; a negative verdict is a
  complete outcome, not a failure.
- [ ] If a field passed, the 10 s textfile sampler publishes it (series name,
  `# HELP`/`# TYPE`, `gpu="card0"` label) with the existing atomic-write and
  write-nothing-on-failure behaviour, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`
  documents the series and its meaning; a test runs the sampler against fixture
  sysfs and asserts its emitted series set exactly matches the set the
  documentation table lists (so docs and behaviour cannot drift). If no field
  passed, no new series is added and the test asserts the sampler's series set is
  unchanged.
- [ ] The pinned-counter guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
  (`FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`) is extended so a saturated activity field cannot
  appear as a utilisation input — `gpu_busy_percent` always, and the
  `gpu_metrics` activity fields when the verdict is negative — with a regression
  test that fails if any `monitoring/*.yaml` rule expression or the probe's own
  utilisation expressions select one.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, docstrings, `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` and
  `monitoring/README.md`; the probe's re-measure procedure (how to re-run the
  capture after a kernel, firmware or driver change) is documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- **No new daemon, port or scrape job.** Reuse `gpu-metrics.service` →
  node_exporter textfile collector; the sampler's 10 s cadence and Prometheus's
  15 s scrape interval are the resolution floor and must be stated as such.
- **Host state is part of the deliverable.** The sampler script lives in
  `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` and is documented in
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`; any change to its series must be reflected
  there so a clean clone can reproduce it.
- **Repository boundary.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (`gpu_busy.py`,
  `reporting.py`) is not edited — adopting a passing field in the daily report is
  a follow-up item, mirroring the constraint recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W.
- **The layout must be pinned in-repo.** The struct is not shipped in the
  installed `linux-headers` packages on this host, so the field table must be
  transcribed with a cited source (`struct gpu_metrics_v3_0`) and validated
  against the observed 264-byte `structure_size`; it must fail closed when the
  kernel reports a different revision.
- **No instantaneous claims.** The values are SMU time-filtered with an
  undocumented window; the output must say so rather than imply per-second
  fidelity.
- **Read cost.** One 264-byte sysfs read per sample; world-readable, no root, no
  ROCm userspace, no `amd-smi`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. v3.0 decoder (field table + header
  validation), paired sampler for `gpu_metrics` + hwmon power + `gpu_busy_percent`,
  band statistics and the pass/fail verdict; CSV and `--json` output.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. Decoder fixtures (real 264-byte
  capture, truncated, unknown revision), fixture-sysfs sampling, verdict
  arithmetic and boundary cases (power exactly 60 W / 90 W, activity exactly
  90 %).
- `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` — New. One committed real capture so the
  layout assertion is reproducible.
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` — Record the verdict, the decode layout and
  (conditionally) the new series; extend the verification section with the probe
  command.
- `monitoring/README.md` — Add `gpu_metrics` to "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi`
  or `amdtop`?" with the measured band statistics; note the re-measure recipe.
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` — Header comment records the `gpu_metrics`
  verdict (no rule change expected; the power rule stays authoritative).
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`
  so saturated activity fields are rejected as utilisation inputs.
- `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` — Only if a field passed: emit the new
  series from the same atomic write.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: the premise is false.** Intake evidence already shows
  `average_gfx_activity` saturated at 100 % from 42 W to 123 W. Mitigation: the
  negative verdict is an explicit, accepted outcome (AC4) and the probe records
  which fields *do* discriminate (DRAM bandwidth, GFX power) for a follow-up.
- **Risk: decoder drift after a kernel or firmware upgrade.** Mitigation: header
  validation plus a committed real capture; the probe refuses unknown revisions
  and the docs carry the re-measure procedure.
- **Risk: undocumented APU field semantics.** `average_gfx_activity` may mean
  "GFX domain powered" rather than "GFX busy" on SMU 14. Mitigation: the bar and
  band statistics decide it, and the interpretation limits are documented.
- **Risk: a capture that misses one band.** A verdict computed only from idle
  samples would be meaningless. Mitigation: AC3 requires both bands, and the
  probe reports per-band sample counts so a one-sided capture is visible.
- **Risk: scope creep** into report integration, new daemons or a full GPU
  telemetry redesign. Mitigation: those are explicit constraints/follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption:** amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` remains the reference compute
  signal (idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W) per
  LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; this item does not re-derive the threshold.
- **Assumption:** the discrimination bar (≥ 30 pp separation, r ≥ 0.6, ≤ 10 %
  idle false-busy) is strict enough — it is far stricter than
  `gpu_busy_percent`'s measured 45.2 % false-busy — and is recorded here so the
  producer can tighten or relax it before implementation.
- **Assumption:** both bands occur on this host within a short window (intake saw
  idle at 42–66 W and compute at 90–123 W within ~15 minutes), so a 30-minute
  capture is sufficient; longer captures are supported by the same CLI.
- **Assumption:** priority stays `high` — the verdict decides whether a direct
  hardware utilisation measure is possible at all on this host, which the usage
  report's honesty goal depends on — even though the likely outcome is a short
  negative report rather than a code change.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL** — Evaluate `amd-smi` as the GPU utilisation source
  (completed). Quantified `gpu_busy_percent`'s saturation (45.2 % false-busy,
  r = 0.28) and filed this item as the remaining avenue. Parent context.
- **LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W** — Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation
  history (in review). Owns the *workload* half (per-slot busy/idle, in-flight
  tasks, the `gpu_utilisation.py` CLI). **Partial overlap only**: that item
  attributes power to llama-server slots; this one judges a *hardware* activity
  field. No CLI or slot work is duplicated here — this item produces a probe and
  a verdict, and its publication step (if any) extends the existing sysfs
  sampler.
- **LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT** — Monitoring: deployable, tailnet-exposed Prometheus
  with honest GPU utilisation (completed) and children: LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48
  (power-derived utilisation rules), LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G (docs for the deployed
  stack). The sampler, units and docs this item extends.
- **LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP** — Fix GPU-wedge false positives (completed):
  established that `gpu_busy_percent` is unusable and power is the
  discriminating signal; the proxy's wedge detector was disabled because of it.
- **LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T** — Grafana dashboard GPU VRAM panel queries series no
  exporter publishes (in progress): the precedent for asserting *published*
  series against documentation, which AC5 reuses.
- **LP-0MVNWULLI006ZYXX** — Cross-check report slot-time against llama-server
  eval timings (independent): the other half of validating the report's busy
  figures.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the post-flip window measured against the ≥24 h pre-flip
baseline and a keep/rollback verdict recorded, so the sweep is judged by its
own flip criteria instead of by assumption.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers the evaluation half of parent AC1
(trigger, observation window, verdict) and AC3's "run the report and record the
numbers".

## Nature of the task

This is a **scheduled measurement task, not code work**. It starts only after
the sweep child has shipped to `dev`, been released, and the proxy has been
restarted in a quiet window. It is expected to stay open for the 7-day
observation window; it must not be implemented inside a code session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger, window, flip criteria and rollback, verified against the
   deployed state before the flip is announced.
2. Preconditions verified and recorded on this item: the reservation endpoint
   is live, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline exists (report/baseline child), the
   sweep is deployed (config 30 s / depth 2 active after a quiet-window
   restart), and the flip is announced in a comment with the restart
   timestamp.
3. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` is run over the 7-day post-flip
   window (≥1 000 queue events), with numbers recorded: dead wait per hour vs
   baseline, residual wins as a share of queue events, remote dispatch volume
   change, ticket-backed dispatch count, and the lease-active vs `none` loss
   split.
4. A keep/rollback verdict is recorded against the three flip criteria —
   ≥50 % fall in dead wait per hour, residual wins ≥20 % of queue events,
   remote dispatch volume rise <20 % relative. A rollback reverts the two
   values to 60 / 8, restarts the proxy, and records the observed numbers.
5. If the window is incomplete (fewer than 1 000 queue events, a log-coverage
   gap, or no restart yet), the item stays `blocked`/`open` with the shortfall
   and the missing days stated — never a verdict from partial data.

## Key Files

- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (consumed)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (rollback only)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sweep child (30 s / depth 2 deployed) and the report/baseline
  child (baseline + tool).

Spun out of `LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R` (contention-queue sweep) as a **top-level,
standalone measurement item** on 2026-10-31 (operator decision), so the sweep
parent can reach `in_review` at code-complete while this scheduled observation
runs on its own calendar. Recorded as `discovered-from:LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R`;

restart that loads 30 s / depth 2). If the release/restart lands later than
2026-10-31, this date moves with it: the item is runnable on restart date + 7
days, and never earlier than ≥ 1 000 post-flip queue events (AC5 forbids a

# Log the resolved snapshot and sidecar paths in `slot_ratio_seed`

## discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want each `slot_ratio_seed` line to carry the snapshot path it
resolved (or the candidate paths it tried) and whether the sidecar was present,
so the remaining per-session cause of `missing_sidecar` / `missing_snapshot` is
attributable from logs instead of inferred from code inspection.

## Why (evidence)

The verdict on LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (docs/dev/slot-ratio-seed-verdict-LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3.md)
proved from 4,488 decisions that the seed path always fails at the lookup
(`missing_sidecar` 75.8 %, `missing_snapshot` 24.2 %; `found`, `expired`,
`prefix_mismatch` all 0). It identified two provable writer-side gaps (the
eviction save path writes no sidecar; the request path skips the sidecar when no
usage block was measured) but could not split the 31 affected sessions between
them, because `missing_sidecar` records `stored_messages=0` by design and logs
neither the resolved `slot_<session>.bin` path nor the sidecar path.

## Scope

**In scope:** one extra field on the existing INFO line (behaviour-neutral) plus
tests/docs. **Out of scope:** any change to the credit decision, `prefix_matches`,
the TTL, or the sidecar format (those belong to LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E).

## Proposed change

1. In `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, extend `log_seed_outcome()` with an
   optional `slot=<basename>` field (basename only — no absolute paths in logs)
   and pass the resolved candidate for `missing_sidecar` / `missing_snapshot`,
   so a later grep can tell which directory/endpoint variant resolved.
2. Cover every outcome branch in `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`.
3. Document the extra field in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every `slot_ratio_seed` line names the resolved snapshot basename (or the
  first candidate tried when none exists), covered by a unit test per branch.
- No behaviour change: the existing outcome vocabulary and credit decision are
  untouched, and the full seed-outcome test suite passes.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the field.

- discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (verdict could not split the
  `missing_sidecar` sub-causes from logs)
- feeds: the post-fix re-measurement on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E

# Proxy: refresh stale client-facing refusal strings for local-preferred deferral

discovered-from:LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 (docs pass; the strings are code, so this item must not change them).

## Goal

Update the two client-facing refusal strings that still describe the pre-deferral
`local-only` semantics, so the remedy the proxy advertises matches the shipped
`local-preferred` contract documented in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## What is stale

- `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`, the `suggested_action` for
  `retryable: false`): still ends with "or send X-Local-Preference: prefer-local to
  allow a remote fallback". After LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE a `too_large` `local-preferred`
  request is already promoted to the remote tiers automatically, so that clause is
  redundant for a pin-local client and misleading for a `prefer-local` one (which
  falls through without any preference change). The compaction half (compact to
  `budget_tokens` and resend) is correct and should stay.
- The deferral 429 body `detail` in `_build_local_only_refusal_response()`: still
  reads "X-Local-Preference: local-only forbids remote fallback" — a deprecated
  spelling, and a description that contradicts the retryable deferral the same
  response now carries.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` names the compaction remedy and the token target, and
  no longer tells the client to change its preference to reach a remote tier.
- AC2 The deferral 429 `detail` names `local-preferred` (or no preference value at
  all) and describes the deferral rather than an unconditional refusal.
- AC3 The strings stay consistent with `proxy/docs/routing.md`'s per-reason retry
  contract (`suggested_action`, AC2 of LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57) — a doc-contract or
  unit test pins the wording/remedy so it cannot drift again.
- AC4 Full suite green at the dev-push gate.

## Constraints

- Strings only: no routing, timing or refusal-shape behaviour change.

## Problem

`proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py::TestCitationsStillResolve` has produced a
**critical `test-failure` work item four times in two days**:

| Item | Created | Cited symbol that drifted |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MVS0CU4V006FLLC | 2026-10-28 | `router.py::_get_local_max_concurrent_queries` 150 → 152, `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` call site 1264 → 1304 |
| LP-0MVREECR9009UN78 | 2026-10-28 | `router.py` citations again |
| LP-0MVSFCP59004XXCG | 2026-10-28 | `router_helpers.py` 2697 → 2764, 2370 → 2430 |
| LP-0MVTHCT8W003VAGE | 2026-10-29 | `router_helpers.py` 2430 → 2631, 2764 → 2965 |

Each item's only change is renumbering `file:line` citations in
`docs/dev/slot-snapshot-pool-sizing-LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5.md` and the matching
`CITATIONS` tuples in the test. No cited behaviour changed in any of the four
occurrences — only line numbers moved.

## Why it keeps happening

The test pins **absolute line numbers** for 36 citations and tolerates
`CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE = 60` lines of drift. Every unrelated commit inside
`proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
(a 6,415-line module that grows fastest of the three) shifts the cited symbols.
Headroom is already thin as of 2026-10-29: `proxy/proxy/router.py:152`
(`def _get_local_max_concurrent_queries`) sits at **drift 55 of 60** — roughly five
inserted lines above it in `router.py` reddens the tree again. The `provider.py`
citations sit at a uniform drift of 16.

Verification (plan session 2026-10-29, read-only): all 36 citations resolve; max
drift 55 (`router.py:152`), next 25 (`provider.py:6127`), next 16 (`provider.py` ×6).

## Options (producer to choose — do not pre-empt)

- **A. Symbol-anchored citations (recommended).** The doc cites `file` + symbol
  (e.g. `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`effective_per_slot_threshold`)) without a line
  number, and the test asserts the symbol exists in that file (and, where useful,
  that the occurrence is unique / inside the expected enclosing definition). A move
  inside a file can no longer fail the suite; removal or rename still does.
- **B. Generated citation index.** Keep line numbers but stop hand-maintaining them:
  a small script derives each cited line from the symbol and rewrites the doc block;
  the test (or a check step) runs the generator and fails only if the committed
  block differs from regenerated output — a one-command fix instead of a new
  critical work item.
- **C. Raise/parameterise tolerance.** Cheapest, but knowingly keeps the treadmill;
  it also weakens the check (a symbol that genuinely moves far away is no longer
  caught). Acceptable only as a stopgap.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 The sizing-doc citation check can no longer fail solely because a cited symbol
  moved *within* its file: a test moves a synthetic symbol down a synthetic source by
  more than the current tolerance and asserts the check still passes.
- AC2 The check still fails when a cited symbol is removed or renamed in its file
  (guard test, mirroring the existing `test_missing_symbol_is_reported`).
- AC3 All existing citations are migrated to the chosen scheme, in the same commit as
  the scheme change (`docs/dev/slot-snapshot-pool-sizing-LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5.md` +
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py`), with no cited behaviour dropped.
- AC4 The doc remains readable by an operator: each citation still names a file and a
  symbol precise enough to locate the behaviour by search (no bare "see provider.py").
- AC5 The decision (option A/B/C with rationale) is recorded on this item, including
  what happens to `CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE`.
- AC6 Full project test suite passes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- No production behaviour change; docs + test only.
- Do not weaken the check into a no-op — AC1/AC2 must both hold.
- The test's doc-table fidelity assertions (`TestProductionGeometry`,
  `TestDocTableFidelity`) are out of scope and must stay green.

## Key Files (verified 2026-10-29)

- `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py` — `CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE`,
  `_resolve_citation()`, `TestCitationsStillResolve.CITATIONS`, `TestCitationDriftGuard`.
- `docs/dev/slot-snapshot-pool-sizing-LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5.md` — §1 nine-behaviour table
  (rows 1–9 carry the 36 citations).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`,
  `proxy/proxy/session.py`, `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`, `proxy/proxy/capacity_admission.py`,
  `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`, `proxy/config.yaml`, `start-llama.sh`,
  `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` — cited sources (read-only for this item).
data.title: Durable fix for the recurring pool-sizing doc citation-drift test failures

## Problem

The automated code-quality review (epic LP-0MVTJXBKO00843I8, tag `Refactor`) filed three work items — one CRITICAL, one HIGH, one MEDIUM — against `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`, a **gitignored, untracked** local analysis scratch script:

- LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA (critical, F401 unused `sys`)
- LP-0MVTJXC1D003NS8F (high, E401 multiple imports on one line)
- LP-0MVTJXCCL008DOEO (medium, I001 unsorted import block)

`.worklog/` is excluded by `.gitignore` (rule `.worklog/`, confirmed with `git check-ignore -v`), and `ruff` itself honours `.gitignore` on directory recursion. Findings on untracked scratch files cannot be remediated by a commit, so each becomes a verification-only no-op item — scheduling noise, and a CRITICAL-tagged one competes with real defects in `wl next`.

## Root cause

The review scan enumerates files by explicit path (or walks the tree without honouring `.gitignore`), so gitignored paths enter the lint scope.

## Proposed fix

- Scope the scan to git-tracked files (`git ls-files`), or add explicit exclusions for gitignored paths / `.worklog/`.
- Optionally suppress findings whose file is untracked (no committable remediation path exists).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The code-quality review emits no findings for files excluded by `.gitignore` (verified by a scan covering `.worklog/analysis/` and observing no findings for it).
- [ ] A regression check covers the scan scope (test or documented scope assertion).
- [ ] No severity inflation: a finding on a gitignored path is either not filed, or filed at `low` with an explicit "untracked scratch file" note.

## Provenance

Discovered while implementing LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA (no-op verification close of the F401 finding for the same gitignored file).

# Intake Brief — Early-released local dispatch keeps prefilling in `llama-server` and starves the next dispatch

## Problem statement

The Option D early release (LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN) detours the client in under a
second, but it does not demonstrably stop the work it abandoned at
`llama-server`: in the measured 24 h window **285 of 1 092 backend prompt
evaluations (26 %) were never consumed by a proxy stream**, and **58 of 60**
residual `prefill_deadline` evictions started inside an *estimated*
abandoned-prefill window. Each fake-warm dispatch therefore appears to cost a
release *plus* a 120 s residual: the retry — which returns to the same
session-pinned slot — reports no prefill progress for its whole lease and is
evicted in turn.

The premise cannot be taken as given. Intake-time log inspection
(2026-10-31, current `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log`) found 143
`Connection handling canceled` events, of which 49 could be joined to a task
id; **only 4 were followed by any further `prompt processing progress` line,
each at most one batch**, and none reached `prompt eval time` after the
cancel. The upstream cancel implemented by LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB does take
effect — so the *magnitude* (26 % of compute, 667 s median backlog) and the
*mechanism* (abandoned work runs to completion) must be decided on evidence
before a fix is chosen. That decision is AC1.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Owns the prefill-deadline and eviction metrics
  and pays for cloud fallback; needs the 26 % waste and the 1.96 user-class
  evictions/h explained and reduced, and needs the residual counts to stop
  being re-attributed every measurement cycle.
- **Agent sessions (herdr workers, `pi` sessions).** They are the retries: a
  dispatch starved behind abandoned work ends as a 503 detour, a longer
  latency, or a failed audit run.
- **Measurement analyst.** Re-runs
  `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py`; needs each release
  joined to the backend task it cancelled, so "prefills computed and thrown
  away" is a measurement and not the subtraction of two unrelated counters.

User stories:

- As an operator, when the proxy releases an accepted local dispatch early, I
  want the GPU work it abandoned to stop within a bounded, recorded time — and
  I want to see that bound in the logs — so compute is never thrown away
  silently.
- As an agent session, when my request is retried after an early release, I
  want it either to prefill immediately (on a free slot) or not to be admitted
  at all, rather than burn a 120 s lease with zero measured progress.
- As an analyst, I want the abandoned-prefill estimate to state its own
  provenance and error, so the 58/60 and 26 % figures are either confirmed or
  restated with evidence rather than quoted as fact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Mechanism decided (confirmed or refuted) with recorded evidence.**
  A committed record under `docs/dev/` (for example
  `docs/dev/abandoned-prefill-release-cancel.md`) reports, for a ≥24 h window,
  per post-acceptance release: release reason, proxy release timestamp, joined
  backend task id (where a join exists), whether a backend cancel was observed,
  the number of `prompt processing progress` lines after the cancel, the time
  from cancel to `slot release: … stop processing`, and whether a
  `prompt eval time` line was emitted for that task. The record states a
  verdict for each competing mechanism below, with the log lines that decide
  it, and either confirms or restates the 26 % (285/1 092) and 58/60 figures:
  - **H1 — the abandoned prefill runs to completion.** Discriminator: cancel
    events followed by many progress batches, and `prompt eval time` emitted
    for a cancelled task. *Intake sample argues against this (4 of 49, ≤1
    batch each) — it must still be measured over 24 h, not assumed.*
  - **H2 — the cancel lands only at a batch boundary.** Discriminator:
    cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution against observed
    `batch.n_tokens` (up to 8 192) at the measured prompt-eval rate (current
    log p10/p50/p90 = 86 / 158 / 536 tok/s), i.e. a bounded tail of roughly
    6–52 s rather than minutes.
  - **H3 — the 26 % is an accounting artefact.** Discriminator: reconcile
    `prompt eval time` (backend, *all* consumers) against
    `Stream finished … provider=local` (proxy) per hour, and enumerate
    non-proxy consumers of `llama-server` (direct calls in `scripts/`,
    benchmarks, health probes) that would be counted as "thrown away".
  - **H4 — the retry is queued behind a draining slot.** Discriminator:
    `slot launch_slot_` time for the retry task versus the abandoned task's
    `slot release`, joined through the proxy's session→slot assignment
    (`_slot_id_for_session` keeps a session on its slot, so a retry returns to
    the slot it abandoned).
  - **H5 — the residual is capacity, not starvation.** Discriminator: the
    event's prompt size and measured prompt-eval rate against the 120 s
    deadline (median event is a 78 213-token prompt; at 158 tok/s a full
    re-prefill is ≈495 s, at 536 tok/s ≈146 s), and whether any later dispatch
    of the same prompt ever reached `progress = 1.0`.

- **AC2 — The release's effect on the backend is bounded and observable.** A
  committed analyser (extend
  `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` or add a sibling)
  joins proxy post-acceptance releases to backend task lifecycles over a ≥24 h
  window and emits: releases with no observed backend cancel (count and
  share), the cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution, and the tokens
  actually evaluated after the cancel. Every release whose cancel cannot be
  joined is reported as unjoined rather than dropped. Target (assumption to
  confirm): **≤ 5 % of releases with no explained backend stop**, and a
  recorded p90 stop latency bound.

- **AC3 — The next dispatch is not starved by abandoned work.** In a
  post-change ≥24 h window (restart-segmented, from on-disk logs), the share
  of `prefill_deadline` events whose dispatch start falls inside an
  abandoned-prefill window falls from **58/60** to a recorded target
  (assumption: **≤ 20 %**), **and** no accepted dispatch expires its lease
  with zero `prefill_progress_measured` while its session's slot is still
  draining an abandoned task — either the retry is routed to a free slot, or
  it observes prefill progress inside its lease. Both halves must be reported;
  a bare `prefill_deadline` count can be gamed by reason conversion (248
  `measured_cache_deficit` releases in the same window).

- **AC4 — No warm-path or throughput regression.** Against the matched
  pre-change window: local completions per hour and large-warm completion
  latency (p50/p90) are not reduced, and `measured_cache_deficit` releases per
  hour do not rise, measured per
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md`. Both windows are reported, with the
  deltas, not just a verdict.

- **AC5 — Tests and documentation.** Hermetic tests pin the new
  release→cancel accounting and any routing/accounting behaviour change (no
  live `llama-server` dependency). Documentation is updated to reflect the
  change, including code comments, `proxy/docs/routing.md` (the abandoned
  dispatch section), `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`, the
  `abandoned_prefill_windows()` docstring in the analyser (which currently
  asserts the opposite of `routing.md`), and
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md` where the baseline moves. The full
  project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Out of scope (owned elsewhere, do not re-tune):** the prefill deadline
  (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds=120`), the cold-prefill budget
  (`local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens=25000`), the admission ladder's warmth
  pricing (LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27), and the slot count (LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5).
- **`llama-server` exposes no cancel API.** Cancellation is only observable as
  a closed socket, and the backend acts on it at its next socket write, so the
  effective granularity is one `n_batch` (up to 8 192 tokens observed). Any
  batch-size (`-ub`/`--batch-size`) change is a backend-config change and must
  be justified by AC1 evidence as a recorded decision — not tuned silently in
  this item.
- **No overlap with the annotation work.** LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM and its child
  LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK own the abandoned-slot identity/annotation
  (`abandoned_busy`, registry entries on every release path, including the
  Option D path's missing `abandoned_slot_id`); this item owns the
  *behaviour* — does the backend stop, and is the next dispatch starved.
  Implementation must not duplicate or contradict that annotation, and the
  Option D plumbing gap is reported to those items rather than fixed here.
- **Measurement integrity.** `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S = 43.1` in the
  analyser prices the abandoned backlog; the measured prompt-eval rate on the
  current log is p10 86 / p50 158 / p90 536 tok/s, so the 667 s median backlog
  estimate is likely overstated several-fold. Any correction must be recorded
  as a measurement change with its own evidence, and the 58/60 figure restated
  on both the old and the corrected basis (backwards comparable) rather than
  swapped.
- **Measurement windows** are ≥24 h, restart-segmented, derived from on-disk
  logs only (no in-process counters), per the existing
  `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md` method.

## Existing state

- **The upstream cancel already exists.** LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (with
  LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK) made every abandonment path close the captured upstream
  stream through `_release_unserved_dispatch`, and records the abandoned slot
  identity for the status annotation. `proxy/docs/routing.md` claims the
  cancel is real: 42 of 82 `Connection handling canceled` events on 2026-10-28
  cancelled a task that never reached `prompt processing done`.
- **The Option D path does not use that plumbing.** In `proxy/proxy/router.py`
  the `MeasuredCacheAbortDetourError` handler calls
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch(...)` **without**
  `upstream_stream_cm` or `abandoned_slot_id` (the deadline path at
  `router.py:2220` passes `upstream_stream_cm=cm`), then closes the stream and
  client itself. So the 42/82 evidence was taken on a different code path than
  the one that produces most of the 389 post-acceptance releases, and the
  abandoned-slot annotation is not recorded for the Option D releases (that
  annotation gap is LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK's scope; here it is evidence, not
  work).
- **The analyser's model contradicts `routing.md`.**
  `abandoned_prefill_windows()` documents "A released dispatch is **not**
  cancelled at `llama-server`" and prices the *whole* remaining prompt
  (`tokens / 43.1`) as backend occupancy — the source of the 667 s median and
  of the 58/60 overlap figure.
- **Session→slot affinity makes the retry return to the draining slot.**
  `_slot_id_for_session` (`proxy/proxy/session.py`) keeps a session on its
  assigned slot, so the immediate retry after a 503 targets the same slot the
  release just abandoned. `slot_id=unknown` on every post-F4 eviction line
  means slot-level attribution is currently unavailable from the eviction log
  alone (it must be reconstructed from `launch_slot_`/`slot release` pairs).
- **Current live counts (intake sample).** `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`
  (3.7 h, 2026-10-31 00:41 → 04:21) holds 39 `local_eviction_after_acceptance`
  events; `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` holds 143 cancels, 121
  completed prompt evaluations and 34 batches of 8 192 tokens.
- **Queue-wait work overlaps but is a different question.**
  LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR / LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5 diagnose why *queue* waits expire
  at the 60 s budget (blocker class, guard projection); this item is about
  accepted dispatches starved by abandoned work they were never told about.

## Desired change

1. Decide H1–H5 on 24 h evidence and publish the decision record (AC1), with
   the 26 % / 58-of-60 claims confirmed or restated.
2. Make the release's backend effect attributable per dispatch (AC2), so
   "abandoned" stops being an estimate derived from a token-rate constant.
3. Remove the starvation path found by AC1 — at minimum: a retry must never be
   admitted into a slot that is still draining work the proxy itself abandoned
   without that fact being visible to admission and to the eviction log
   (AC3). The specific mechanism (route to a free slot, hold the dispatch out
   of "about to prefill" pricing, or bound the wait against the drain) is a
   decision for AC1's evidence, not for intake.
4. Prove no warm-path or throughput regression (AC4), and leave the
   documentation and tests consistent with the new measurement (AC5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — the `MeasuredCacheAbortDetourError` handler
  (≈ lines 1998–2120) and the deadline handler (≈ lines 2190–2260); the Option
  D release currently omits `upstream_stream_cm` / `abandoned_slot_id`.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`, `_record_abandoned_slot`,
  `_abandoned_slot_lookup`.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_slot_id_for_session` / `_slot_owners` (session
  affinity is what sends the retry back to the draining slot).
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` —
  `abandoned_prefill_windows()`, `backend_prefill_accounting()`,
  `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S`.
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`,
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — the three
  records whose claims must agree after the change.
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_measured_cache_abort*.py` — the existing hermetic
  coverage the new tests sit beside.

## Related work

- LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O — the measurement item that produced the 26 % / 58-of-60
  evidence (`discovered-from` parent of this item).
- LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (completed) and LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK (completed) — the
  upstream cancel + abandoned-slot registry whose effectiveness this item
  re-verifies for the Option D path.
- LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2 (completed) — regression test: abandoned dispatch not
  reported saturated.
- LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM (in progress) — annotate the post-cancel release lag so a
  draining slot is never reported saturated. Adjacent, not overlapping.
- LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK (blocked) — record and re-verify abandoned slot identity
  on every release path (including the unattributable
  `measured_cache_deficit` polls). Owns the annotation gap this item records as
  evidence.
- LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN — Option D early release (the release under test).
- LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 — warmth pricing (out of scope here).
- LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5 — slot count (out of scope here).
- LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR, LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5, LP-0MVV29X2E004INFL — abandoned
  *queue-wait* share diagnosis; same abandonments, different question.
- LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK — post-deadline re-dispatch fix measurement window (its
  restart precondition applies here too: a post-change window needs the proxy
  restarted onto the fix).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (AC3 target):** ≤ 20 % of `prefill_deadline` events starting
  inside an abandoned-prefill window, plus zero zero-progress starvations.
  Chosen because a hard zero cannot be promised while the backend's stop
  granularity is one batch; confirm at review.
- **Assumption (AC2 target):** ≤ 5 % of releases with no explained backend
  stop. Confirm at review.
- **Assumption (scope):** a `--batch-size` change is out of scope for the fix
  and, if AC1 shows the batch tail dominates, is recorded as a follow-up work
  item rather than tuned here.
- **Assumption (refutation path):** if AC1 refutes H1 and the 26 % proves to be
  an accounting artefact, this item stays open and re-scopes to the mechanism
  the evidence supports (H3 + H4/H5); the refutation plus the corrected
  estimator is the deliverable, and the item is not closed on the refutation
  alone.
- **Risk — stale evidence transfer.** The 42/82 cancel evidence was taken on
  the deadline path, not the Option D path; AC1 must not reuse it as proof.
- **Risk — reason conversion games the metric.** A reduction in
  `prefill_deadline` can be produced by more `measured_cache_deficit` releases;
  AC3 therefore counts both reasons and AC4 bounds the latter.
- **Risk — measurement window invalidated by a restart.** A post-change window
  requires the proxy to be restarted onto the fix; if it is not, the window
  measures the old code (the exact failure recorded in LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Batch-size tuning, deadline/budget re-tuning, warmth
  pricing, slot-count changes and queue-budget modelling are all *linked work
  items*, never extra scope here.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: What numeric target counts as "the next dispatch is not starved"
  (AC3)?** — *Not asked interactively; no blocking answer required.*
  **Default adopted at intake:** ≤ 20 % of `prefill_deadline` events starting
  inside an abandoned-prefill window, plus zero dispatches expiring with no
  `prefill_progress_measured` while their slot drains abandoned work.
  Source: intake reasoning from the measured 58/60 baseline and the
  batch-granularity constraint (a hard zero is unprovable while the backend
  stops only at a batch boundary). Producer may adjust at review.
- **Q: Is a `llama-server` batch-size (`-ub`/`--batch-size`) change in scope
  if AC1 shows the batch tail dominates the waste?** — **Default adopted at
  intake:** out of scope for this item's fix; recorded as a decision in AC1 and
  filed as a follow-up work item if the evidence supports it. Source: the
  item's own scope note ("make the release cancel or bound the abandoned
  backend work") plus the standing rule against re-tuning deployed knobs
  without new evidence.
- **Q: If AC1 refutes the "prefill runs to completion" premise, does this item
  close on the refutation?** — **Default adopted at intake:** no; the item
  re-scopes to the mechanism the evidence supports and keeps AC3's starvation
  target as the closure gate. Source: the item already frames AC1 as
  "confirmed or refuted", and a refutation that leaves 1.96 user-class
  evictions/h unexplained would leave the operator's question unanswered.
- **Research note (duplicate check).** `wl search prefill`, `wl search
  "abandoned prefill"`, `wl search cancel`, `wl search starv` and
  `wl search ghost` were run. No completed item satisfies this item's ACs:
  LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB implemented the cancel but did not verify it per
  dispatch or address the starved retry; LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM annotates the
  draining slot but does not change behaviour. The description was therefore
  re-scoped to the *difference*: per-dispatch cancel accounting, the Option D
  path's missing plumbing, and the starvation of the retry.
- **Research note (log sample, 2026-10-31).** `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log`:
  143 `Connection handling canceled`, 49 joinable to a task id, 4 with any
  `prompt processing progress` after the cancel (≤ 1 batch each), 121
  `prompt eval time` lines, 34 batches of `batch.n_tokens = 8192`; prompt-eval
  rate p10/p50/p90 = 86 / 158 / 536 tok/s. `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`
  (3.7 h) holds 39 `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events. Method: `grep`
  plus a task-id join script over the live log; reproducible from the log
  files named above.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK** – Record and re-verify abandoned slot identity on every release path (blocked)
- **LP-0MSB0RV72001KNRV** – Slot registry leak: _cleanup_stale_local_dispatch never frees _slot_owners entries (completed)
- **LP-0MQS6MPWE005NJJA** – Phase 3: Session invalidation → slot release (completed)

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: abort, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+436 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: abort, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+436 more)
