## Finding

The proxy's log retention (7 days: `logging.retention_days` default in
`proxy/proxy/utils.py:1034`, which makes `TimedRotatingFileHandler` keep
`backupCount = 7 × 24 / 6 = 28` six-hour segments, with `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy`
as a `rotate 7` daily safety net) is shorter than the age a committed
measurement record reaches before it is audited or re-examined.

Concrete instance: `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` had to restate the pre-change baseline
on the window `2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `2026-10-29 00:10:18` (8 days before the
implementing session). The window was measured in full on 2026-10-30, but by
2026-11-05 the first ~16 h of `2026-10-28` had been pruned: only
`proxy.log.2026-10-28_16.gz` (16:16:14→22:16:12) and
`proxy.log.2026-10-29_001015.gz` (00:00:00→00:10:15) survive — **6 h 10 m of a
24 h window (25.7 %, 67 of 136 enqueued waits)**. The committed record
therefore carries two provenance classes (measurement-time full window vs
today's coverage re-measurement) instead of a single regenerable artefact.

This is a recurring shape, not a one-off: any "measure a window, then commit a
record" slice that lands more than ~7 days after its window has to be
documented as un-reproducible, and every AC of the form "re-running the
embedded command regenerates the committed JSON" degrades to "regenerable
while the archives survive".

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want a measurement window to stay re-derivable for
at least as long as the records that quote it, so a committed record can be
re-checked by a later session instead of being taken on trust.

## Options (not a decision — intake should choose)

1. **Raise `logging.retention_days`** (e.g. 7→14 or 30). Cheap in disk: measured
   on 2026-11-05, `/var/log/llama-proxy` holds 46 `proxy.log*.gz` archives
   totalling **42 MB** (≈0.9 MB per six-hour segment), so doubling or
   quadrupling retention costs tens of MB, not GB. The knob already exists
   (`logging.retention_days`). Costs: more files in one directory (check
   `prune_logs` startup scan time) and the logrotate drop-in's `rotate 7`
   safety net must be raised to match, or it will prune what the in-process
   handler retains.
2. **Archive the window's archives with the record** — a `--emit-archives`
   mode or a documented `tar`/`rsync` step alongside a record commit. Larger
   repo footprint (or an external artefact store), but makes the record
   self-contained forever.
3. **Record the harness output as the artefact of authority** and drop the
   "regenerates byte-for-byte" expectation from records older than retention —
   documentation-only, no code change; what `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` does today.

## Acceptance criteria (draft, for intake)

- AC1: A documented retention window is at least as long as the longest-lived
  measurement record the project commits, with the value stated in
  `docs/dev/` and pinned by a test.
- AC2: A measurement record older than the retention window is either
  reproducible from a committed/archived artefact, or the record states its
  provenance classes explicitly (no silent re-derivation claim).
- AC3: Disk cost of the chosen retention is measured, not assumed, and stated
  on the host-install/retention doc.

## Evidence

- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-diurnal-baseline.md`
  ("Provenance and coverage") — the coverage map and the pruning mechanism.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` (`setup_logging`, `prune_logs`,
  `logging.retention_days` default 7).
- `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` (`rotate 7`, `size`-free daily safety net).
- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` — rotation/decompression discovery (unaffected;
  the loss is retention, not discovery).
data.title: Proxy log retention (7 days) is shorter than the records that quote measured windows

data.description:
discovered-from: LP-0MW3K7XJ30027RV6

## Observed (2026-11-05, while verifying the backend OOM ranking)

Starting the host-direct path (`./start-llama.sh router`, the `llama_allow_host_fallback` route) fails immediately:

```
$ /usr/local/bin/llama-server --version
/usr/local/bin/llama-server: error while loading shared libraries: libmtmd.so.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

$ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64 /usr/local/bin/llama-server --version
ggml_cuda_init: found 1 ROCm devices (Total VRAM: 122880 MiB)
version: 8782 (e97492369)
```

`/usr/local/lib64/libmtmd.so.0` exists, so the binary is fine — that directory is simply not on the loader path (no `ld.so.conf.d` entry) and `start-llama.sh` does not add it.

## Why it matters

`proxy/config.yaml` sets `llama_allow_host_fallback: true`, and host-first startup is attempted before the configured (podman) script. Today that attempt always fails and only logs a warning before falling back, so the host route is dead weight and a host-only deployment cannot start a backend at all. Latent, not urgent: the deployed path is the podman wrapper, which carries its own libraries.

## Suggested minimal fix

- Put `/usr/local/lib64` on the loader path in the install/refresh path (`ld.so.conf.d/llama.conf` + `ldconfig` from `install_proxy.sh`/`scripts/rebuild-llama.sh`), or export `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64` in `start-llama.sh` when the directory exists.
- Report a broken host binary at install time instead of only when the fallback is exercised.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `start-llama.sh <model>` starts the host `llama-server` without an externally supplied `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
- **AC2** — The install/rebuild path detects and reports a host binary that cannot load its libraries.
data.title: Host llama-server binary cannot start: libmtmd.so.0 not on the default library path

## Goal

Produce a **proposal** (no implementation without explicit producer approval) for separating audit/bulk traffic from interactive user traffic at the shared local gate.

**Discovered from:** LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I. Rec 5 of the root-cause analysis. **This item must not change code, config or the running proxy.**

## Why it matters (measured, certified window 2026-11-06 14:15:50 → 2026-11-08 00:00)

- **20 of the 60** `prefill_deadline` events are audit sessions (`audit-*`), with 44k–103k prompts; 11 audit events are attributed capacity and 9 predicted-warmth.
- Audit is excluded from the (b2) user-class criterion, **but not from its cause**: audit prefills occupy the shared gate and the second slot, and the measured cold rate swings **235–295 tok/s (contended) vs 530–770 tok/s (best case)**.
- Audits raise the occupancy class (9/60, 15 %, and under-counted while `/slots` times out), i.e. they make *user* events miss even though their own events are not counted.

## Scope

**In:** a written proposal in `docs/dev/` (or an appendix to the existing prefill/admission docs) covering options, costs and the decision criteria.

**Out:** any implementation, config change, deployment or proxy restart. Implementation happens only in a follow-up item created **after** producer approval.

## Options the proposal must cost

1. **Audit remote-only** (or audit-on-a-different-provider): zero local audit load; cost = remote tokens/latency.
2. **Idle-gated local access for audits**: local only when the pool has been idle ≥ N s; needs a measured N.
3. **Priority-weighted gate**: user `high`/`medium` pre-empts queued audit prefills; needs the priority plumbing already present (LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI).
4. **Per-class deadline**: audits get a shorter local deadline (e.g. 60 s) and fall back sooner.
5. **Do nothing** — with the measured cost stated.

For each: expected effect on the user-class rate, on local coverage/utilisation, on remote spend, and the risk.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Proposal written.** A document states each option, its mechanism, the measured evidence it rests on, expected effect on the user-class combined rate (baseline 2.223/h; target ≤ 0.5/h), local coverage, and remote cost. It names a recommendation and the decision criteria.
- **AC2 — No implementation.** The item changes **no** source, config or runtime state; git diff is empty apart from the proposal document (or the doc lives in the work item description if a doc is premature). No proxy restart is performed by this item.
- **AC3 — Impact model reproducible.** The projected numbers come from a stated, reproducible computation over the certified window dataset (`/tmp/ac3-window-2026-11-06.json`, recorded on LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) — e.g. "remove audit events → X user events remain, Y/h", with the command/analysis recorded.
- **AC4 — Producer approval gate.** `needsProducerReview` is set on creation; the item advances only when the producer records approval (a comment naming the chosen option). Until then it stays `idea`/`intake_complete` and dispatchable-for-proposal only.
- **AC5 — Follow-up on approval.** On approval, create the implementation item (issue type `feature`, high) carrying: the restart AC (proxy restarted via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` with PID/HEAD/`/health` evidence), the dated-title re-anchor AC, and the impact measurement. Link it here with `related`/`depends-on` as appropriate.
- **AC6 — Proxy restart AC (deferred, not waived).** This item performs no restart. The restart it is accountable for is the one in the approved follow-up: that follow-up must restart the proxy and record old/new PID, start time, deployed HEAD and `/health` before its impact measurement. If the producer rejects the proposal, state explicitly that no restart is owed and close.
- **AC7 — Dated titles.** The dated-title re-anchor (`\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` in open titles) is owed by the approved follow-up's restart; this item records that obligation and, on rejection, notes that no re-anchor is triggered.

## Relationship

- Related: LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (serialise audits at the shared local resource), LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI (batch work must send a priority header so interactive sessions are protected), LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 (early-released local dispatch starvation).
- The producer's (b2) re-scope conversation (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) should consider this proposal as one of the levers.
data.title: [proposal] Separate audit and bulk traffic from interactive user traffic at the local gate (no implementation without approval)

## Goal

Report the prefill-deadline residual with a **stall-weighted rate** and stall percentiles, so a fast `measured_cache_deficit` detour (0.2–25 s, sometimes < 1 s) is not counted as equivalent to a 180 s `prefill_deadline` stall.

**Discovered from:** LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I. Rec 7 of the root-cause analysis.

## Why (measured, certified window 2026-11-06 14:15:50 → 2026-11-08 00:00)

- The producer's (b2) criterion is a **rate of post-acceptance evictions** (user-class combined 2.223/h vs ≤ 0.5/h). It treats every event equally regardless of cost.
- `measured_cache_deficit` is the **working** early detector of warm mispricing: user events p50 **24.9 s**, p90 127 s, max 175.5 s, and **12 of 47 under 1 s**. `prefill_deadline` is always **180.0–181.0 s**.
- Consequence: making aborts faster (the intended fix direction) leaves the rate unchanged, so the metric cannot reward the improvement. It also hides the real user-visible cost (Σ stall seconds), which is what the residual is about.

## Scope

**In:** `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` and the daily usage report (`report.md` + `--json`): add the stall-weighted rate, stall percentiles, and a sub-second-abort count; definitions section; additive schema; a verification run on the certified window.

**Out:** any change to admission, routing or the deadline itself; any change to the (b2) rate definition (that is the producer's call — this item supplies the missing numbers so the re-scope can be decided with evidence).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Stall-weighted rate.** The analyser and the daily report publish `stall_seconds_per_hour = Σ elapsed_s / window_hours`, split by reason and by user/audit, alongside the existing per-event rate.
- **AC2 — Percentiles.** Publish p50/p90/p95/p99 stall seconds per reason, and the count and share of events with `elapsed_s < 1 s`, `< 5 s`, `≥ deadline − 1 s`.
- **AC3 — Definitions.** The report's definitions/appendix states explicitly that `measured_cache_deficit` aborts and `prefill_deadline` stalls are not equivalent, and why (early detour vs full-deadline wait), with the measured p50/p90 evidence.
- **AC4 — Additive `--json`.** The JSON gains a `stall_cost` block; existing keys keep their names, meanings and types (schema compatibility test).
- **AC5 — Verified on the certified window.** Running against 2026-11-06 14:15:50 → 2026-11-08 00:00 reproduces: combined user-class rate 2.223/h, plus the stall-weighted value, p50/p90/p95/p99, and the sub-second count. Numbers recorded in the item and in the report.
- **AC6 — No proxy behaviour change.** The change is reporting-only; the proxy's decision paths and logs are untouched (assert with a test that the analyser consumes the existing log fields only).
- **AC7 — Build and tests.** Build clean; changed-scope tests green via `/skill:test`; full suite at the dev-push gate; a golden-file test for the rendered report section.
- **AC8 — Proxy restart.** After merge, restart the proxy via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` so the deployed tree, CLI and analyser are provably the same commit; record old/new PID, start time, deployed HEAD and `/health`. No behaviour change is expected from this restart; state that explicitly.
- **AC9 — Dated titles updated at that restart.** Re-anchor every open work item whose title contains a date (`\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`) to the new restart, or state why unchanged; list them in a summary comment (12 at creation: LP-0MVZ4R2B20027XK3, LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K, LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57, LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1, LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q, LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6, LP-0MVZRRGD40005T0A, LP-0MW0JCFMM0000DM2, LP-0MW3K7Z7T0094JK6, LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8, LP-0MW0S88WJ005SBPH, LP-0MVT114SV004P2PI) — plus the new validation items once they exist.

## Relationship

- Extends LP-0MW2SQNHJ0044PV6 (wasted-compute section in the daily report) and reuses LP-0MVW8S8OZ00449YR's analyser.
- The producer's (b2) re-scope (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) should use these numbers to choose between a rate target and a stall-cost target.

## Goal

Turn the window dataset into the honest verdict the producer asked for — per-reason rates, the combined user-class rate and a stall-weighted rate that does not treat a 0.5 s `measured_cache_deficit` detour as equivalent to a 180 s deadline stall (parent AC5).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC5 — Verdict, with the honest split.** Report (a) per-reason user/audit rates; (b) the combined user-class rate; (c) the **stall-weighted** rate (Σ`elapsed_s`/h) and p95/p99 stall seconds — the metric that distinguishes a 0.5 s `measured_cache_deficit` detour from a 180 s deadline stall; (d) attribution; (e) the count of admissions refused by the new deadline-capacity bound. State met/not-met against ≤ 0.5/h combined **and** against the stall-weighted target agreed with the producer. **Resolved stall-weighted target:** a **≥ 90 % reduction in user-class Σ`elapsed_s`/h versus the group-1 window**, recomputed with the same analyser command over the group-1 dataset (producer decision, 2026-11-08, Appendix Q1).
- **AC2 — Per-reason and combined rates.** Report the per-reason user/audit rates for every post-acceptance eviction reason side by side with the group-1 window, plus the combined user-class rate.
- **AC3 — Stall-weighted method.** At planning time `analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` has no `stall_cost` block (that is the unscheduled chore LP-0MW7V30AZ007JB5Z), so compute Σ`elapsed_s`/h from the `--json` event list (split by reason and user/audit, with p95/p99 and the count/share of events under 1 s, under 5 s and ≥ deadline − 1 s); reuse the analyser block only if it has landed by run time, and record which path was used.
- **AC4 — Attribution and capacity refusals.** Report the attribution split (occupancy / capacity / predicted-warmth), the share of admitted prompts whose residency was unmeasured, and the count of admissions refused by the new deadline-capacity bound shipped by LP-0MW7V2D13004ZO65, naming the exact log reason/field it publishes (state explicitly if the count is only derivable from the pre-existing `prefill_budget_exceeded` reason).
- **AC5 — Verdict committed.** Commit the verdict report as `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-group2-verdict.md` and comment the headline numbers on this item; publish the absolute s/h values for both windows so the ≥ 90 % ratio is auditable.

## Constraints

- Reporting-only: no proxy behaviour change in this child.
- If a number cannot be produced from the dataset, say so explicitly and name the missing field — do not substitute an estimate silently.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-group2-24h.json`
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-group2-verdict.md`
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py`

## Deliverables

- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-group2-verdict.md` — both verdicts plus the supporting numbers — committed to `dev`
- Verdict summary comment on this item

## Earliest date/time for implementation

**2026-11-07T14:16Z** — the measurement window anchor plus 24 h.

Per the shared convention in [`docs/dev/measurement-windows.md`](docs/dev/measurement-windows.md) (LP-0MVWC0FAT0018PMW):

- **Window anchor** = the proxy restart that loaded the rung. That is the running process
  (`.venv/bin/python3 -m uvicorn proxy.server:app`, pid 2634864, `ps -o lstart` **2026-11-06T14:15:50Z**, log line
  `2026-11-06 14:15:50`). Independent confirmation that this start loaded the rung: the interpreter compiled
  `proxy/proxy/__pycache__/provider.cpython-312.pyc` at **14:15:52** and that bytecode contains the
  `local_last_resort*` symbols; the rung had merged to `dev` as `52130e54d` on 2026-11-05 05:48, ~32 h earlier.
- **Window start** = the first whole minute after that restart → **2026-11-06T14:16Z**.
- **Earliest the window can close** = window start + 24 h → **2026-11-07T14:16Z**.

That instant has passed (the same anchor already serves LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K, LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8 and
LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q, all of which quote `2026-11-06T14:16Z → 2026-11-07T14:16Z`), so this item is actionable
immediately — the date above is a floor, not a start signal.

Two further constraints:

- **The window must be restart-free.** A restart inside it (`start-proxy.sh --restart`, a deploy, a crash
  recovery) re-anchors it: a partial window never yields a PASS. Confirm with `ps -o lstart` on the uvicorn pid
  and by grepping the window's logs for `Starting LLama Proxy Server`. Coordinate with the shared calendar
  before any deploy.
- **Act before ≈ 2026-11-13.** `logging.retention_days` is 7 (`proxy/config.yaml`), so the post-deploy segments
  (`proxy.log.2026-11-07_*`, `proxy.log.2026-11-08_*`) are pruned roughly 7 days after the deploy. Past that
  the window must be re-based on a fresh deploy (`docs/dev/proxy-usage-evidence-windows.md` covers archiving
  the raw segments first).

## Goal

As the proxy operator, I want the ≥ 24 h post-deploy evaluation of the last-resort local admission rung (AC8 of LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W) performed and recorded, so that the rung is either confirmed to reduce `All providers exhausted` failures inside idle gaps without a regression in prefill evictions/discarded tokens, or is killed/retuned with the measured evidence.

## Why this is a separate item

AC8 of LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W is a *post-deploy* criterion: it cannot be satisfied by code, tests or documentation, only by a measurement window taken after the rung has been running in production. The implementation item delivered the rung, the tests and the measurement surfaces (`docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` → "Last-resort rung (LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W): the post-deploy measurement"); the actual window belongs here.

Baseline to beat (measured 2026-10-29 23:43:30 → 2026-10-30 23:43:30, *before* the rung existed):

- 236 of the window's 686 `All providers exhausted` warnings (34%) occurred inside 13 GPU-idle gaps carrying 98 inbound requests and 0 streams.
- The idle-admit ladder fired 1,337 times and refused 1,291 (96.6%) on `prefill_budget_exceeded`; 292,924 prefill tokens / 44 evictions discarded per 24 h.

## In scope

- Run the usage analysis over a ≥ 24 h window that lies entirely after the deployment instant, e.g.
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-11-06 14:16:00" --end "2026-11-07 14:16:00"` (the CLI supports arbitrary `--start`/`--end`), and repeat for a later restart-free window if the first is inconclusive.
- Attribute every `local_last_resort_admit` line (`estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `idle_seconds`, `threshold_seconds`, `deadline_s`, `warm_cap`, `remote_exhausted=true`, `session`, `turn`) and every `routing_idle_admit_refused` it superseded.
- Read the three comparison surfaces from the same window: `All providers exhausted` inside idle gaps vs the 236 baseline, `local_evictions_after_acceptance` with `reason=prefill_deadline`, and discarded prefill tokens.
- Record the numbers, the window boundaries, the exact commands and the verdict on this item, and bring the result back to LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W (comment, and re-audit that item so its AC8 — now scoped to this handover — stays consistent with the measured outcome).

## Out of scope

- Any code change. If the evaluation shows `local_last_resort_deadline_seconds` too low (rising `prefill_deadline` evictions), the fix is a raised knob value, filed as its own item; if it shows no benefit, the fix is the kill switch (`local_last_resort_idle_seconds: 0`), also its own item.
- Re-measuring remote provider quota/capacity root causes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A restart-free ≥ 24 h window lying entirely after the window start (2026-11-06T14:16Z) is analysed with the deterministic CLI, and the window boundaries, the restart-free evidence (`ps -o lstart` on the uvicorn pid, no `Starting LLama Proxy Server` marker inside the window) and the exact command are recorded on this item.
- AC2: The window's `All providers exhausted` count inside GPU-idle gaps is reported against the 236/686 baseline, with the idle-gap definition and the gap count stated.
- AC3: `local_last_resort_admit` lines in the window are counted and attributed (per-session/per-turn) with their `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `idle_seconds`, `deadline_s` distribution; if the count is zero, the reason is stated (remote chain never empty, prompt above warm cap, or GPU not idle) with the supporting log evidence.
- AC4: `local_evictions_after_acceptance` (`reason=prefill_deadline`) and discarded prefill tokens are reported for the window and compared with the pre-rung 24 h figures (44 evictions / 292,924 discarded prefill tokens).
- AC5: An explicit verdict — **keep** (exhaustions inside idle gaps fell, neither eviction metric rose), **retune** (`local_last_resort_deadline_seconds` too low — quote the distribution) or **kill** (`local_last_resort_idle_seconds: 0`) — recorded on this item with the numbers that justify it, and echoed as a comment on LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W.
- AC6: If the window is inconclusive (no remote-exhaustion episode coincided with an idle GPU), that is recorded explicitly with the evidence and the item stays open for a later ≥ 24 h window — an inconclusive window is never reported as a pass.

## Measurement surfaces

Documented in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` (section "Last-resort rung (LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W): the post-deploy measurement"): `local_last_resort_admit` grep count, `All providers exhausted` inside idle gaps, usage-report `local_evictions_after_acceptance`, and the prefill-token accounting. Knobs and rationale: `proxy/config.yaml` (`local_last_resort_idle_seconds: 300`, `local_last_resort_deadline_seconds: 600`), `proxy/docs/routing.md` → "Last-resort local admission".

## Related

- LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W — last-resort local admission rung (implementation; AC8 handed over to this item)
- LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S — eviction metrics + triage rule
- LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J — idle-admit ladder
- LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D — cold-prefill admission budget
- LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK — post-deadline re-dispatch fix
- LP-0MVWC0FAT0018PMW / `docs/dev/measurement-windows.md` — shared restart-free 24 h window calendar (anchor rule followed here)
- LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K, LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8, LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q — sibling measurements already using this same 2026-11-06T14:16Z anchor
- `docs/dev/proxy-usage-evidence-windows.md` — archive raw segments before rotation ages them out

## Goal

**As** the implementer of the deadline capacity, **I want** the publication and refusal rows written and failing first, **so that** the shipped capacity number, its distinct refusal reason, the measured-residency basis and the rollbacks are pinned before enforcement changes.

Parent AC2 and AC6 (test half). **Test-after** (order swapped per the producer's Q1 precedent, 2026-11-13): this item depends on the `[impl] Deadline token capacity` item (LP-0MW957RB3000ER79), so the implementation lands first and these rows assert the shipped behaviour rather than a failing placeholder (shared test-writing guidelines).

## Scope

Add rows to `proxy/tests/test_deadline_token_capacity.py`: unit rows against `proxy.prefill_eta` (decision + `status_estimate` + the `local_admission_guard` log line, captured with `caplog`) and admission-path rows through the existing provider helpers used by `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`.

**Out:** production code, config changes, docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Capacity is published.** `deadline_capacity_tokens` equals `local_prefill_deadline_seconds / cold_ms_per_token` (integer tokens) and appears on the `/llama/local/status` estimate payload and on the `local_admission_guard` decision log line; a row pins the shipped-config value (180 s at the cold rate) to its derivation, not to a hard-coded number.
- **AC2 — Distinct refusal reason.** A request whose cold projection exceeds the capacity is refused with a documented, distinct reason (not `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`) and falls back to remote; boundary rows at capacity tokens (admitted) and capacity + 1 (refused).
- **AC3 — Cold basis, measured residency honoured.** With residency **unmeasured** the whole prompt is priced cold and a whole-prompt size above capacity is refused; with **measured** residency the measured new tokens are priced, so a large measured-warm prompt (measured new tokens well inside capacity) stays admissible — the parent's warm-prompt guardrail.
- **AC4 — Rollback rows (parent AC6).** `local_admission_guard_policy: observe` logs the would-be refusal and admits; `off` is inert; `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile: 0` derives the capacity from the cold point estimate; each row documents the restored behaviour.
- **AC5 — Fail-open rows.** An uncalibrated cold window, an unreadable capacity or a disabled deadline never manufactures a refusal.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/tests/test_deadline_token_capacity.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`

## Goal

**As** the proxy operator, **I want** the prefill deadline expressed as an explicit **token capacity**, published and enforced at admission, **so that** a prompt that cannot finish inside `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` is refused up front (fast remote fallback) instead of being admitted and evicted after three minutes.

Parent AC2 and AC6 (implementation half).

## Scope

**In:** `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (capacity derivation, decision field, distinct reason, log line), `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (`/llama/local/status` payload), the admission call sites in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` and `proxy/proxy/capacity_admission.py`, `proxy/config.yaml` comments, `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

**Out:** changing `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (a producer decision), the residency threshold rules, slot count/context, the analyser's rate basis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deadline token capacity.** Compute `deadline_capacity_tokens = local_prefill_deadline_seconds / cold_ms_per_token` (about 46 000 tokens at today's rate) from the same cold calibration the guard prices with, publish it on the `/llama/local/status` payload and in the admission log line (the decision carries the field, so the log and the payload cannot drift), and refuse/route-remote any request whose cold prefill (whole prompt when residency is unmeasured) exceeds it, with a distinct, documented reason.
- **AC2 — Enforcement with a distinct reason.** A request whose priced prefill exceeds the capacity is refused at admission with its own documented reason and detours to remote; the bound is applied on **every** admission path the flat cold-prefill cap already guards (queue entry, direct/free-slot dispatch, idle/economic bypass, capacity gate) by reusing those existing enforcement points.
- **AC3 — Cold basis, measured residency honoured.** The capacity is compared against the cold (whole-prompt) projection when residency is unmeasured and against the measured new tokens when the measured prefill record exists, so a measured-warm large prompt is not refused for its prompt size.
- **AC4 — Rollback documented.** `local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off` and a percentile of 0 restore today's behaviour; stated in `proxy/config.yaml` at the setting and in `proxy/docs/routing.md`, and tested — the capacity bound is inert under `off` and log-only under `observe`.
- **AC5 — Interaction stated.** The config and docs state how the capacity relates to `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` (the flat cap stays the tighter bound at 25 000 tokens; the capacity governs whole-prompt cold pricing and any deployment that raises or disables the flat cap).
- **AC6 — Build clean and changed-scope tests green** via `/skill:test` (full suite at the dev-push gate).

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/capacity_admission.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`

## Goal

**As** the analyst, **I want** the two-server eval-line attribution rows written and failing first, **so that** the embeddings server's ~102 tok/s lines can never again pollute the single seconds basis the residual analysis publishes.

Parent AC4 (test half). **Test-after** (order swapped per the producer's Q1 precedent, 2026-11-13): this item depends on the `[impl] Honest seconds basis` item (LP-0MW957SKX0079QKC), so the implementation lands first and these rows assert the shipped attribution contract.

## Scope

Commit a small two-server fixture log and add rows to `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py`. The fixture carries the router spawn lines for both models (`name=Qwen3 on port <n>` and `name=mxbai-embed on port <m>`), interleaved `prompt eval time = … (… tokens per second)` lines from both PIDs, and a rotation-split variant with no spawn line.

**Out:** production code, docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Qwen3-only basis.** The analyser's `seconds_basis_tok_s` on the two-server fixture equals the median of the Qwen3 `prompt eval` rates only (asserted to within 0.5 tok/s), and is materially different from the naive all-lines median (also asserted, so a regression fails loudly).
- **AC2 — Excluded lines are accounted for.** The payload reports the excluded embeddings port(s) and the number of contributing eval lines, so an operator can see why the basis moved.
- **AC3 — Rotation and ambiguity rows.** A fixture whose spawn line was rotated away, with a single unannounced eval-line port, infers the Qwen3 port; a genuinely ambiguous file yields `seconds_basis_tok_s = None` rather than a polluted median.
- **AC4 — Existing rows unchanged.** Rows that legitimately use a single-server fixture keep passing unchanged.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/two_server_llama.log`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py`
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py`

## Goal

**As** the analyst, **I want** `seconds_basis_tok_s` derived only from the Qwen3 local model's `prompt eval` lines, **so that** the residual analysis prices stalls with a rate that describes the model under test.

Parent AC4 (implementation half). Measured: the reported `128.4 tok/s` mixes the embeddings server's ~102 tok/s lines with Qwen3's ~250 tok/s.

## Scope

**In:** `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — attribute each `prompt eval time` line to a model port (spawn line, then single-unannounced-port inference, else unusable) and compute the basis from the Qwen3 lines only; report excluded ports and contributing line counts in the payload; update `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-postchange.md` and the `proxy/docs/routing.md` reference.

**Out:** the admission-side calibration (separate items), the usage-analysis skill's own `build_speed_stats` (already port-attributed — reuse its contract, do not fork it), any change to the eviction model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Port attribution.** Each eval line is attributed to a model port from the router spawn line (`name=Qwen3 on port <n>` / `name=mxbai-embed on port <m>`), falling back to the single-unannounced-port inference; the attribution contract matches `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/llama_log_parser.py`.

- **AC3 — Honest failure.** A file with no identifiable Qwen3 port yields `seconds_basis_tok_s = None` (never a polluted median), and the report says why.
- **AC4 — Two-server fixture green** (the C5 rows pass) and the previously published basis unchanged for single-server windows.
- **AC5 — Docs updated** with the basis rule and the reason it exists.

## Goal

**As** the implementer, **I want** the replay proofs written first against committed fixtures rather than a live recording, **so that** the cold rate, the capacity refusals and the 2026-11-03 mispricing are reproducible from the repository forever.

Parent AC3 and AC10 (test half). **Test-after** (order swapped per the producer's Q1 precedent, 2026-11-13): this item depends on the `[impl] Deadline token capacity` item (LP-0MW957RB3000ER79), so the implementation lands first and these replay proofs assert the shipped bound.

## Fixtures (committed, not live)

- `proxy/tests/fixtures/cold_regime_window_2026_11_06.jsonl` — the certified window's event set (prompt tokens, measured cached ratio, processed tokens, first-byte ms) reduced to the decisive rows, including the 55k/67k/90k predicted-warm events and the measured cold dispatches at 3.81–4.26 ms/token.
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/recorded_sequence_2026_11_03.jsonl` — **reconstructed** from the incident evidence recorded on LP-0MW0KZUUS002LICZ (51 945-byte tool append, 19 628-token prompt, 6 622 cached, 13 006 new, 53.2 s and 72.0 s first bytes). The original recording directory `herdr-1793695298-3654733-20033` has been pruned from `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` (verified 2026-11-09); the fixture header records that provenance and the pruned path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Cold rate within tolerance.** Replaying the certified-window fixture through the real calibration + admission path fits a cold rate within **±20 %** of the measured 3.81–4.26 ms/token (assert both the ms/token and the implied tok/s).
- **AC2 — Replay proof.** A test replays the certified window's event set (or a committed fixture of it) and asserts that the 55k/67k/90k predicted-warm events are refused at admission with the deadline-capacity reason, and that no admitted request had a cold projection exceeding the capacity bound (asserted over every admitted row).
- **AC3 — Incident replay (parent AC10).** The reconstructed 2026-11-03 sequence is priced cold (cached_ratio forced to 0 for the oversized append, already shipped by LP-0MW0KZUUS002LICZ) and refused/routed remote under the capacity bound instead of dispatched and evicted; the row names both the price and the refusal.
- **AC4 — Deterministic and self-documenting.** Each fixture row carries its provenance comment; the harness resets calibration state per test; no row reads a live log or a live recording.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/cold_regime_window_2026_11_06.jsonl`

# ContextHub: Dispatcher uses lease-derived availability

## Goal

Make the herdr downtime dispatcher's capacity decision consume the proxy's lease-derived availability signal (from LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK), not raw version counts or local budget assertions.

**Parent:** LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (Serialise audits at the shared local resource). **Covers:** Parent AC3 (dispatcher uses lease-derived availability), Parent AC5 (ContextHub child item).

## Problem

`ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `getActiveAudit` already consults the machine-scoped dispatch-budget ledger but ContextHub may run on multiple servers, each asserting its own cap. The dispatcher needs a single authoritative signal from the proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Proxy availability query.** `getActiveAudit` (or `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts`) queries the proxy's audit availability endpoint instead of reading local `budget.json`.
- **AC2 — No dispatcher/proxy mismatch.** The mismatch between dispatcher admission and proxy refusal is impossible by construction (both use the same lease-derived availability signal).
- **AC3 — Single-machine limitation recorded.** A ContextHub child item records the single-machine limitation of `~/.herdr/downtime` and the chosen cross-machine mechanism.
- **AC4 — Cross-machine mechanism documented.** The chosen cross-machine mechanism is documented in `machine-coordination.ts`.

- **AC3 — Dispatcher uses lease-derived availability (parent AC3).** The dispatcher's capacity decision uses the lease-derived availability signal (see the sibling lease-occupancy item LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5), not raw version counts, and the mismatch between dispatcher admission and proxy refusal is impossible.
## Deliverables

- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` queries the proxy's audit availability.
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` / `machine-coordination.ts` — cross-machine mechanism.

## Dependencies

- **LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK** — Proxy owns the audit admission budget (provides the availability endpoint).

## Key Files

- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` queries the proxy's audit availability.
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — capacity decision consumes the lease-derived availability signal.
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — audit-tier admission consults the proxy availability instead of the local `budget.json` cap.
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — cross-machine mechanism documentation.

## Goal

Stand up a single top-level **validation project** for the "do not admit infeasible cold prompts" programme (groups 1 and 2), so the post-deploy measurement work has one owner, one tracker and one closure contract — separate from the implementation epics.

This project owns the **evidence that by construction only exists after deployment**: the group-serialised proxy restarts, the post-restart measurement windows, the residual-rate comparison against baseline, and the dated-title re-anchoring that accompanies each restart.

Created to break the circular dependency recorded in the audit of **LP-0MW7V292T0020G02**: that epic's AC7/AC8 require the group-1 restart, while the group-1 validation item `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` `depends-on` that epic. The producer decision is to accept the implementation epic as delivered (AC1–AC6, AC9, AC10 green) and **defer AC7/AC8 to this validation project**.

## Scope

**In:**

- The group-1 validation (`LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4`) and group-2 validation (`LP-0MW7V14DN007F127`) as children.
- Exactly one proxy restart per group, serialised (group 1 before group 2).
- Post-restart measurement windows and the residual/stall-weighted rate comparison against the certified baseline.
- Dated-title re-anchoring at each restart, with the per-item disposition summary.

**Out:**

- Any code or config change (validation items are measurement-only; findings become new work items).
- Additional restarts beyond one per group.
- Changes to the 25k budget / 38k cold / 120k warm thresholds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Group 1 restart + measurement.** Exactly one proxy restart loads group 1 (measured-residency routing `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02`), recording old/new PID, start time, deployed HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> HEAD`) and raw `/health`; the post-restart window measures post-acceptance evictions, `prefill_deadline` user/audit, `measured_cache_deficit` user and the combined rate (target ≤ 0.5/h), and records the result on this project and on LP-0MW7V292T0020G02 (satisfying its AC7). Slot-before-admission (`LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI`) is **not** part of group 1 (2026-11-11 producer decision): it was never implemented when the group's single restart was taken, so its deployed validation is a separate future group, `LP-0MWBZVU04007OII2`.
- **AC2 — Group 2 restart + measurement.** After the group-1 window is recorded, exactly one further restart loads group 2; the residual is measured honestly with the stall-weighted rate and recorded.
- **AC3 — Dated-title re-anchoring.** Each group restart re-anchors every open work item whose title contains a date (`\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`) and posts a summary comment listing each item and its disposition (12 items at creation) — satisfying LP-0MW7V292T0020G02 AC8.
- **AC4 — Measurement-only.** No validation child changes code or config; any regression found becomes a new (discovered-from) work item.
- **AC5 — Build and tests.** No build/test impact expected (measurement-only), but each child records the HEAD it measured and the evidence paths (proxy logs, `/health`, PID).
- **AC6 — Traceability.** Results are cross-linked to the implementation epics so the deferred AC7/AC8 are demonstrably closed here.

## Children

| Group | Child | Covers parent ACs | Current state |
|-------|-------|-------------------|---------------|
| 1 | LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4 — one proxy restart, then measure whether infeasible cold prompts are still admitted | AC1, AC3 (group-1 leg), AC4, AC5 | open / plan_complete (scope: measured-residency `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` only) — restart done (LP-0MW8COT80004L1SR), window 2026-11-10T14:18:26Z → ≥ 2026-11-11T14:18:26Z, **manual run**, hand-off LP-0MW8CS8NY0087XBV |
| 2 | LP-0MW7V14DN007F127 — one proxy restart after group 1, then measure the residual with the stall-weighted rate | AC2, AC3 (group-2 leg), AC4, AC5 | blocked / plan_complete (`run-not-before 2026-11-12T00:00:00Z`); producer hold released 2026-11-11, hand-off LP-0MW8EAWA5000OP5X |
| closure | LP-0MWBLEQ1S003MUTF — parent closure: verify parent AC1–AC6 and cross-link both group verdicts to the implementation epics | AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6 (verification + cross-link) | blocked / intake_complete — depends on both group hand-offs |

### AC ownership

Every parent AC has at least one owning child; the per-group children carry the measurement work and the closure child carries the project-level verification and the cross-link to the implementation epics (AC6 was previously unowned — nothing posted the deferred AC7/AC8 closure on LP-0MW7V292T0020G02). Automated tree-coverage review reports 100% parent-AC coverage (`tree_coverage.py run-coverage-review LP-0MWATML8J003DOCO` → `proceed`).

## Plan: changelog

| When | Change |
|------|--------|
| 2026-11-10T16:29Z | Plan review of the existing decomposition; no new children (both group children already `plan_complete`). |
| 2026-11-11T04:02Z | Re-plan after the stage was reset to `intake_complete`. Added child **LP-0MWBLEQ1S003MUTF** (parent closure, AC1–AC6 verification + implementation-epic cross-link) and its dependencies on both group hand-offs; updated the Children table with AC ownership; re-ran the six review stages and the AC-coverage review (now 100%, `proceed`). |

Group-1 validation `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` lost the obsolete dependency edge and was reset to `open` (Q3). Group 2's `Map` producer hold was released (Q4). The group-1 measurement window is a **manual** operator run at ≥ 2026-11-11T14:18:26Z (Q2), so the project is held with the `Map` assignee. |

## Relationship

- **Implementation epics (work under test):** LP-0MW7V292T0020G02 (measured prefix residency routing, group 1) and LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI (slot-before-admission, group 1).

- Restarts are performed only by the group validation children via `/skill:start-proxy --restart`; this project never restarts anything itself.

  (slot-before-admission) was `open` at `plan_complete` with no commits on any
  ref when the group-1 restart was taken (2026-11-10T14:18:26Z, PID 316897,
  HEAD `01d89a19e`), so it is not part of the deployed group-1 tree. Its
  deployed validation is tracked separately as `LP-0MWBZVU04007OII2` (blocked on
  LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI).
- **Manual scheduling (Q2).** The group-1 measurement window is run manually by

  assignee as a scheduling hold so it is not auto-dispatched; the
  `run-not-before` marker is title-only and is not a real gate.

## Problem
Running `wl doctor upgrade` rewrites the committed `.githooks/pre-push`, `.githooks/post-merge` and `.githooks/post-rewrite` from this repo's committed v4/v2 templates to the ContextHub wl CLI's canonical v3/v1 templates (`PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT`). This is a silent DOWNGRADE: the committed v4 pre-push hook has the pushed-commit guard and emits 'ERROR: no test runner found — ...', which `tests/test_git_hooks.py:428` asserts; the CLI v3 hook emits 'ERROR: run_tests.py not found — ...' and lacks the guard. The downgrade turns the working tree red and would also be a regression if committed.

## Impact
- Discovered while auditing LP-0MW305AJ80085AEK: `wl doctor upgrade` (run to clear a schemaVersion error) left the three hooks dirty, so the full suite failed on `tests/test_git_hooks.py::test_missing_runner_fails_closed_on_dev_push` and the audit's F3 triage created a false-positive test-failure item (LP-0MWC0K2DD0073YML, since closed).
- Any dev push from the dirty checkout would trip the repo's own pushed-commit dirty-tree guard.

## Evidence
- `git diff` on the three hook files reverts committed v4/v2 to the CLI v3/v1 content; the CLI text carries RISE-0MVSS1KVV002TJUL.
- CLI source: /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/dist/doctor/hook-upgrade.js (`PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT`) and dist/commands/doctor/upgrade.js (invokes `upgradeHooks('.githooks', ...)`).
- Fix applied locally: `git checkout -- .githooks/pre-push .githooks/post-merge .githooks/post-rewrite`.

## Desired behaviour
`wl doctor upgrade` must not overwrite a project hook that has evolved beyond the CLI template (or must detect the newer version and no-op), so it can never silently downgrade committed hooks.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `wl doctor upgrade` leaves an already-newer committed hook untouched (no-op), verified by a test.
2. `wl doctor upgrade` does not modify `.githooks/` files whose committed content differs from the CLI template in a way the CLI cannot prove is older.
3. Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Goal

Add an explicit code-repository root to the audit runner so git-derived content (merge gate, file-scope manifest, changed files, green-run evidence, code-quality scope, Phase 2 cwd) resolves independently of the worklog-owning project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `audit_runner.py issue` accepts `--code-root DIR` (CLI, near the existing `--worklog-dir` at `:15480`) and `AUDIT_CODE_ROOT` env var.
2. `_resolve_owning_project_root` / the per-audit root resolution (`per_audit_root = git_root`, `:10832`) honours the explicit code root when given; precedence: `--code-root` flag > `AUDIT_CODE_ROOT` env > today's owning-project default.
3. `_AuditContext.per_audit_project_root` (`:9832`) and all its consumers (`_resolve_code_quality_scope` `:6106`, F3 cwd `:3438`, repo-index fallback `:3559`, debug-log slug `:3755`, remediation re-scan `:12471`) use the resolved code root.
4. `wl` routing is completely untouched: `--code-root` never leaks into `_run_wl`/`resolve_worklog_flags`; `--worklog-dir` keeps governing the worklog.
5. A non-git or non-existent `--code-root` directory is a hard error with non-zero exit and no `pi` call.
6. Read-only mandate preserved: the runner never fetches/checkouts/mutates the code repo it points at.
7. AC1/AC2/AC3 tests pass.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`

**Dependencies:** AC1 test, AC3 test

## Goal

When no explicit code root is given and the item's resolved touched-file set is entirely absent from the owning repo while present in a sibling project, abort with a loud, actionable scope error naming the sibling candidate(s) — before any Phase 1 model call.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Uses `_resolve_touched_files()` (`:2632`) as the touched-file set; id-grep and comment-sha sources yield nothing in the owning repo for a cross-repo item, so Key Files is the deciding contributor.
2. If the touched set is empty/undeterminable the new check is skipped entirely — the existing `_validate_file_scope_manifest` coverage check (`:2013`) stays the backstop; never a false abort.
3. When every touched path is absent from the owning repo but present (at HEAD) in a sibling candidate, abort with an `Audit scope error`-style message naming the candidate(s), non-zero exit, no persisted report, seconds not minutes.
4. Sibling candidate population = `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT/*/.worklog/config.yaml` (same scan as `_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`); per-candidate check is one bounded path-existence check per touched file, never a whole-repo scan.
5. `_verify_launch_context`'s unaffected ownership abort remains intact; same-repo launches are zero-cost (check only runs when the touched set is entirely absent).
6. AC2 test passes.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`

**Dependencies:** AC2 test
